FULL DIRECTORY TREE ``` src/ ├── App.svelte ├── main.js ├── app/ │ ├── router/ │ │ ├── Router.svelte │ │ └── routes.js │ └── stores/ │ ├── auth.js │ ├── org.js │ └── ui.js ├── infrastructure/ │ ├── broadcast/ │ │ ├── BroadcastService.js │ │ ├── BrowserBroadcastService.js │ │ ├── MockBroadcastService.js │ │ └── broadcastManager.js │ ├── crypto/ │ │ └── webCrypto.js │ ├── db/ │ │ ├── db.js │ │ └── schema.js │ └── scheduler/ │ └── timerManager.js ├── modules/ (containing index.js facades for each domain) │ ├── auth/index.js │ ├── customer/index.js │ ├── importExport/index.js │ ├── masterData/index.js │ ├── nlp/index.js │ ├── notification/index.js │ ├── order/index.js │ ├── org/index.js │ ├── risk/index.js │ ├── style/index.js │ ├── template/index.js │ └── ticket/index.js ├── pages/ │ ├── AdminPage.svelte │ ├── CRMPage.svelte │ ├── LoginPage.svelte │ ├── MasterDataPage.svelte │ ├── MessagesPage.svelte │ ├── NLPPage.svelte │ ├── OrdersPage.svelte │ ├── OrgSetupPage.svelte │ └── RiskReviewPage.svelte ├── repositories/ │ ├── base/ │ │ ├── BaseRepository.js │ │ └── IRepository.js │ └── implementations/ │ ├── AuditRepository.js │ ├── CustomerRepository.js │ ├── ImportExportRepository.js │ ├── MasterDataRepository.js │ ├── NLPRepository.js │ ├── NotificationRepository.js │ ├── OrderRepository.js │ ├── OrgRepository.js │ ├── RiskRepository.js │ ├── StyleRepository.js │ ├── TemplateRepository.js │ ├── TicketRepository.js │ └── UserRepository.js ├── services/ │ ├── AuditService.js │ ├── AuthService.js │ ├── CryptoService.js │ ├── CustomerService.js │ ├── ImportExportService.js │ ├── MasterDataService.js │ ├── NLPService.js │ ├── NotificationService.js │ ├── OrderService.js │ ├── OrgService.js │ ├── RiskReviewService.js │ ├── SchedulerService.js │ ├── StyleService.js │ ├── TemplateService.js │ └── TicketService.js └── utils/ ├── constants.js ├── idGenerator.js └── validation.js ``` --- ### 2. FULL CONTENT: Services #### **AuthService.js** (Complete) Local-only authentication with session management, password hashing (PBKDF2 with 310k iterations), guest trial (30 mins), inactivity auto-lock (10 mins), password change with key rotation, and RBAC. Uses BroadcastChannel for multi-tab synchronization. Methods: `login()`, `logout()`, `createGuestSession()`, `resetInactivityTimer()`, `lockSession()`, `unlockSession()`, `createUser()`, `changePassword()`, `deactivateAccount()`. Fully implemented. #### **CryptoService.js** (Complete) Facade for WebCrypto operations. Holds in-session CryptoKey (cleared on lock/logout). Methods: `hashNewPassword()`, `verifyPassword()`, `deriveSessionKey()`, `clearSessionKey()`, `isUnlocked()`, `encrypt()`, `decrypt()`, `rotateEncryptedFields()` (for password changes), `deriveBackupKey()`, `resolveBackupKey()`, `encryptBackup()`, `decryptBackup()`, `maskValue()`. Fully implemented. #### **CustomerService.js** (Complete) Manages customer records with encrypted sensitive fields (allergies, material restrictions, stored value). Methods: `createCustomer()`, `updateCustomer()`, `adjustStoredValue()` (with delta, blocking negative), `adjustPoints()`, `addRating()` (running average), `revealSensitiveFields()`, `getMaskedFields()`, `getByOrg()`, `getById()`. Fully implemented with validation. #### **AuditService.js** (Complete) Append-only logging. Stores never overwritten during standard imports. Methods: `log()` (immutable entries), `getEntityHistory()`, `getActorHistory()`, `getSince()`. Fully implemented. #### **ImportExportService.js** (Complete) Encrypted backup/restore with schema version validation. Protected stores (sessions, auditLogs) not exported. Methods: `exportBackup()` (JSON blob, encrypted), `previewImport()` (returns diff without applying), `applyImport()`, `validateSchemaVersion()`. Fully implemented. #### **MasterDataService.js** (Complete) Versioned master data lifecycle (Color, Size, Season, Brand, Supplier, Style). One active version per (entityType, organizationId). Optimistic concurrency (version conflict detection on publish). Methods: `publishVersion()`, `getActiveVersion()`, `getVersionHistory()`, `getAllActiveVersions()`. Fully implemented. #### **OrderService.js** (Complete) Order lifecycle with restriction flags (allergies, material restrictions). Validates transitions per ORDER_TRANSITIONS map (Draft → Placed/Canceled → In Progress/Canceled → Ready/Canceled → Completed). Methods: `createOrder()`, `transitionOrder()`, `getByCustomer()`, `getOrderDetail()` (with events), `getByStore()`. Fully implemented. #### **OrgService.js** (Complete) Organization hierarchy (Company → Factory → Store → Warehouse). Validates parent-child type pairing, enforces single-parent, prevents deletion of non-leaf nodes. Methods: `createNode()`, `updateNode()` (name only, no structural changes), `deleteNode()` (leaf only), `getTree()`, `getSubtree()`, `getScopedNodeIds()`, `validateParentChildType()`. Fully implemented. #### **StyleService.js** (Complete) Style SKU management. References Color, Size, Season, Brand, Supplier (all must be active). Prevents deactivation-reference violations. Methods: `createStyle()`, `updateStyle()`, `deactivateStyle()`, `getByOrg()`, `getByStore()`. Fully implemented with reference validation. #### **TicketService.js** (Complete) After-sales ticket lifecycle (Open → In Progress → Resolved → Closed). SLA tracking with auto-overdue marking. Terminal states (Closed) prevent further transitions. Methods: `createTicket()`, `assignTicket()`, `transitionTicket()`, `evaluateOverdue()` (batch marks overdue), `getOverdue()`, `getTicketDetail()` (with event history), `getByCustomer()`, `getByStore()`. Fully implemented. #### **TemplateService.js** (Complete) Message template management with placeholder detection and validation. Compact template length enforcement (≤160 chars). Methods: `createTemplate()`, `updateTemplate()`, `renderTemplate()` (variable substitution + compact validation), `deleteTemplate()`, `getByOrg()`, `getById()`. Fully implemented. #### **NotificationService.js** (Complete) Multi-channel notification queue (in-app only for offline). Deduplication via idempotency keys (source key + minute bucket). Retry schedule [1, 5, 15 minutes], max 3 retries. Methods: `upsertChannel()`, `subscribe()`, `enqueue()`, `processDueItems()`, `getInbox()`, `markRead()`. Fully implemented. #### **RiskReviewService.js** (Complete) Risk case evaluation via machine rules, sensitive word matching, bidding heuristic analysis. Rule types: `field_contains`, `field_exceeds`. Methods: `loadSensitiveWordDictionary()`, `evaluateRules()`, `validateImage()`, `evaluateBiddingHeuristics()` (frequency + fingerprint clustering), `assignCase()`, `resolveCase()`, `dismissCase()`, `getInbox()`. Fully implemented. #### **SchedulerService.js** (Complete) Multi-tab leader election with heartbeat-based failover (TTL 10s). Reconciles missed work on startup. Methods: `registerTask()`, `start()` (immediate reconciliation + leader election), `stop()`. Fully implemented with BroadcastChannel coordination. #### **NLPService.js** (Complete) Offline NLP workspace: TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification, lexicon-based sentiment analysis, dictionary-based NER, entity disambiguation. Methods: `importText()`, `runBatch()`, `runIncremental()`, `getRunHistory()`, `getRunDetail()`, `createValidationProfile()`. Fully implemented with algorithmic processors. --- ### 3. FULL CONTENT: Repositories #### **Base Layer** **IRepository.js** Interface contract. Throws if any method called on base class. Enforces: `create()`, `findById()`, `findAll()`, `findByIndex()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `clear()`, `count()`. **BaseRepository.js** IndexedDB CRUD implementation. Constructor takes `storeName`. Methods: - `_readStore()`, `_writeStore()` (tx helpers) - `create()`, `findById()`, `findAll()`, `findByIndex()`, `findOneByIndex()`, `findByCompoundIndex()`, `update()`, `delete()`, `clear()`, `count()`, `createMany()`, `upsert()` #### **Implementation Layer** **UserRepository.js** Store: `users`. Methods: `findByUsername()`, `findByOrgNode()`, `findByRole()`. **AuditRepository.js** Store: `auditLogs`. Methods: `findByActor()`, `findByEntityType()`, `findByEntity()`, `findSince()` (timestamp-based filtering). **CustomerRepository.js** Store: `customers`. Methods: `findByOrg()`, `findByMembershipTier()`. **MasterDataRepository.js** Store: `masterDataVersions`. Methods: `findActiveVersion()` (single per entity type/org), `findVersionHistory()`, `findActiveVersionsByOrg()`, `atomicVersionSwitch()` (transactional deactivate + activate). **OrderRepository.js & OrderEventRepository.js** Stores: `orders`, `orderEvents`. Methods: `findByCustomer()`, `findByStore()`, `findByStatus()` (Order); `findByOrder()` (Events). **OrgRepository.js** Store: `organizations`. Methods: `findByParent()`, `findByOrganization()`, `findByType()`. **StyleRepository.js** Store: `styles`. Methods: `findByOrg()`, `findByStore()`, `findActiveStylesReferencingEntity()` (reference-check for deactivation). **TicketRepository.js & TicketEventRepository.js** Stores: `tickets`, `ticketEvents`. Methods: `findByCustomer()`, `findByStore()`, `findByStatus()`, `findByAssignee()`, `findOverdue()`, `findDueForOverdueCheck()` (SLA eval) (Ticket); `findByTicket()` (Events). **TemplateRepository.js** Store: `templates`. Methods: `findByOrg()`, `findCompactByOrg()`. **NotificationRepository.js** (4 repositories) - `NotificationChannelRepository`: Store `notificationChannels`. Methods: `findByOrg()`. - `NotificationSubscriptionRepository`: Store `notificationSubscriptions`. Methods: `findByUser()`, `findByEventType()`. - `MessageQueueRepository`: Store `messageQueue`. Methods: `findByStatus()`, `findDueForRetry()`. - `NotificationRepository`: Store `notifications`. Methods: `findByUser()`, `findUnreadByUser()`. **RiskRepository.js** (4 repositories) - `RiskRuleRepository`: Store `riskRules`. Methods: `findActiveByOrg()`, `findByEntityType()`. - `RiskCaseRepository`: Store `riskCases`. Methods: `findByOrg()`, `findByStatus()`, `findByReviewer()`, `findBySourceType()`. - `BidEventRepository`: Store `bidEvents`. Methods: `findByUser()`, `findByFingerprint()`, `findByItemInWindow()` (time-window frequency analysis). - `LinkedAccountRepository`: Store `linkedAccounts`. Methods: `findByPrimaryUser()`, `findByLinkedUser()`, `findAllLinksForUser()`. **ImportExportRepository.js** Not extending BaseRepository (operates across multiple stores). Methods: `exportAll()` (all non-protected stores), `importAll()` (replaces all non-protected stores), `previewDiff()` (add/update/delete diff). **NLPRepository.js** (3 repositories) - `ImportedTextRepository`: Store `importedTexts`. Methods: `findBySourceType()`, `findUpdatedSince()`. - `ValidationProfileRepository`: Store `validationProfiles`. Methods: `findByModelVersion()`, `findLatest()`. - `NLPRunRepository`: Store `nlpRuns`. Methods: `findByOrg()`, `findLatestByOrg()`. --- ### 4. FULL CONTENT: Utilities #### **constants.js** Centralized constants: - **Organization**: ORG_NODE_TYPES (company, factory, store, warehouse), VALID_PARENT_CHILD map - **Roles**: ROLES (administrator, store_manager, analyst, reviewer, guest) - **Master Data**: MASTER_DATA_ENTITY_TYPES (color, size, season, brand, supplier, style) - **Membership**: MEMBERSHIP_TIERS (Bronze, Silver, Gold) - **Orders**: ORDER_STATUSES, ORDER_TRANSITIONS (state machine) - **Tickets**: TICKET_STATUSES, TICKET_PRIORITIES, TICKET_EVENT_TYPES - **Messages**: QUEUE_STATUSES (Draft, Queued, Sent, Failed), RETRY_SCHEDULE_MINUTES ([1, 5, 15]), MAX_RETRIES (3) - **Risk**: RISK_CASE_STATUSES, OUTCOME_CODES (no_issue, warning_issued, content_removed, account_link_confirmed, suspicious_activity_confirmed, false_positive) - **Validation**: PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (12), REASON_NOTE_MIN_LENGTH (10), ALLERGY_MAX_CHARS (500), COMPACT_NOTICE_MAX_CHARS (160), MAX_IMAGE_BYTES (5MB), RATING (1-5), STORED_VALUE_DECIMALS (2), GUEST_TRIAL_MINUTES (30), AUTO_LOCK_MINUTES (10), DEFAULT_TICKET_SLA_HOURS (48) - **Crypto**: PBKDF2_ITERATIONS (310k), PBKDF2_HASH (SHA-256), AES_ALGORITHM (AES-GCM), AES_KEY_LENGTH (256), IV_LENGTH_BYTES (12), SALT_LENGTH_BYTES (32), ALGORITHM_VERSION ('v1') - **NLP**: F1_ALERT_THRESHOLD (0.7), RUN_TYPES (batch, incremental) - **Image**: ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME (PNG, JPEG), magic byte arrays #### **validation.js** Input validation functions: - `validatePassword()`: ≥12 chars, ≥1 digit, ≥1 symbol - `validateReasonNote()`: ≥10 non-whitespace chars - `validateAllergyField()`: ≤500 chars - `validateStoredValue()`: Non-negative, max 2 decimals - `validatePoints()`: Non-negative integer - `validateRating()`: Integer 1–5 - `validateCompactNoticeLength()`: ≤160 chars post-substitution - `extractPlaceholders()`: Regex `{name}` extraction - `validatePlaceholders()`: All declared placeholders have values - `renderTemplate()`: Variable substitution (throws on missing) - `validateImageFile()`: MIME type + magic bytes + size check - `isValidOutcomeCode()`, `isValidMembershipTier()`, `isValidRole()`, `isValidTicketPriority()`: Set membership checks #### **idGenerator.js** ID generation: - `generateId()`: UUID v4 (cryptographically random) - `generatePrefixedId()`: `{prefix}_{timestamp_base36}_{random6}` (human-readable, sortable) - `generateIdempotencyKey()`: `{sourceKey}__{minuteBucket}` (minute-level deduplication) --- ### 5. DATABASE INFRASTRUCTURE #### **schema.js** IndexedDB schema definition. DB_NAME='retailops_console', DB_VERSION=1. SCHEMA_STORES object with 29 stores: - **Auth**: users (username unique), sessions (expiresAt index) - **Org**: organizations (parentId, organizationId, type indexes) - **Master Data**: masterDataVersions (compound by_entityType_orgId, isActive, orgId indexes) - **Inventory**: styles (by_orgId, by_sku, by_storeId, by_isActive), colors, sizes, seasons, brands, suppliers, warehouses - **Customer**: customers (by_orgId, by_membershipTier) - **Orders**: orders (by_customerId, by_orgId, by_storeId, by_status), orderEvents (by_orderId, by_type) - **Tickets**: tickets (by_customerId, by_orgId, by_storeId, by_status, by_assignedTo, by_isOverdue), ticketEvents (by_ticketId, by_type) - **Notifications**: notificationChannels (by_orgId, by_isEnabled), notificationSubscriptions (by_userId, by_channelId, by_eventType), templates (by_orgId, by_isCompact), messageQueue (by_orgId, by_status, by_recipientUserId, by_nextRetryAt), notifications (by_userId, by_read, by_createdAt) - **Import/Export**: importedTexts (by_sourceType, by_sourceId, by_updatedAt) - **NLP**: validationProfiles (by_modelVersion, by_createdAt), nlpRuns (by_orgId, by_runType, by_modelVersion, by_createdAt) - **Risk**: riskRules (by_orgId, by_targetEntityType, by_isActive), riskCases (by_orgId, by_status, by_assignedReviewerId, by_sourceType), bidEvents (by_orgId, by_userId, by_itemId, by_deviceFingerprint, by_createdAt), linkedAccounts (by_orgId, by_primaryUserId, by_linkedUserId) - **Audit**: auditLogs (by_actorId, by_entityType, by_entityId, by_createdAt), appConfig (by_orgId unique) PROTECTED_STORES: sessions, auditLogs (never cleared during import). #### **db.js** IndexedDB access module. Singleton pattern (_db cached). Functions: - `initDB()`: Opens/creates DB, runs schema upgrade via _applySchema() - `getDB()`: Returns cached instance (throws if not initialized) - `closeDB()`: Closes and clears cache (test cleanup) - `isDBInitialized()`: Boolean check - `requestToPromise()`: Wraps IDBRequest in Promise - `withTransaction()`: Read-write transaction helper with rollback - `withReadTransaction()`: Read-only transaction helper --- ### 6. APP LAYER (Routing & State) #### **app/stores/auth.js** Svelte writable stores: `currentUser`, `isLocked`, `isAuthenticated`, `isGuest`. Derived stores: `currentRole`, `isAdmin`. Functions: `syncAuthStores()`, `clearAuthStores()`. #### **app/stores/org.js** Svelte writable stores: `selectedOrg`, `selectedStore`, `orgTree`. Derived: `companyNodes`, `storeNodes`. Functions: `persistSelectedStore()`, `restoreSelectedStore()` (LocalStorage-backed). #### **app/stores/ui.js** Svelte writable stores: `currentPath`, `isLoading`, `toast`, `tableColumnLayouts`, `sidebarCollapsed`. Functions: `navigate()`, `showToast()` (auto-dismiss), `saveColumnLayout()`, `restoreColumnLayouts()` (LocalStorage-backed). #### **app/router/routes.js** Route map: `/login`, `/org-setup`, `/master-data`, `/crm`, `/orders`, `/messages`, `/nlp`, `/risk-review`, `/admin`. DEFAULT_ROUTE='/login'. PUBLIC_ROUTES (no auth required): {'/login'}. ROLE_ROUTES map restricts access by role. #### **app/router/Router.svelte** Hash-based routing. `resolvePageComponent()` enforces auth + role checks, redirects unauthorized access. ## Phase 2 Output Report

### A. Implemented Features

**AuthService**
- Login lockout: 5 consecutive failures → `lockoutUntil` set (15-min). Counter resets on success.
- `createUser` initializes `failedLoginAttempts: 0, lockoutUntil: null`

**CustomerService**
- Full RBAC (`STORE_MANAGER+` for write, `ANALYST+` for reveal)
- Org-scope enforcement: non-admin users restricted to their `organizationNodeId`
- `createCustomer`, `adjustStoredValue` (credit/debit/negative-balance enforcement), `revealSensitiveFields`, `getMaskedFields`

**MasterDataService**
- Optimistic concurrency via `expectedActiveVersionId` (throws `Concurrency conflict` on stale)
- `publishVersion` requires `STORE_MANAGER+` with org-scope check
- `ANALYST` cannot publish; `STORE_MANAGER` blocked from cross-org publish

**OrgService**
- create/update/delete require `ADMINISTRATOR`
- Read ops require authentication

**NotificationService**
- New `notifyUser(userId, {type, title, body})` — direct system notification without template
- `getInbox` enforces own-inbox-only for non-admin
- `markRead` enforces own-notification-only
- `upsertChannel` requires `STORE_MANAGER+`

**OrderService**
- Terminal state guard (COMPLETED, CANCELED): prevents re-transition
- Notification triggers on IN_PROGRESS, READY, COMPLETED, CANCELED via `notifyUser(...).catch(() => {})`

**TicketService**
- Notification on `assignTicket` (notifies assignee)
- Notification on `transitionTicket` (notifies assignee when different from actor)

**RiskReviewService**
- `evaluateRules` requires `STORE_MANAGER+`
- `assignCase`/`resolveCase`/`dismissCase` require `REVIEWER+`
- `resolveCase`: requires non-empty `outcomeCode` and non-empty `resolutionComment`
- `dismissCase`: requires non-empty comment; sets `FALSE_POSITIVE` outcome code
- Already-closed cases throw `already closed` on any modification attempt
- `ingestBidEvent`: validates positive `bidAmount`; stores bid event record
- `evaluateBiddingHeuristics`: flags when item bid count within window exceeds threshold
- `ingestLinkedAccount`: validates `primaryUserId !== linkedUserId`

**ImportExportService**
- ADMINISTRATOR-only for all operations
- Export encrypts full snapshot (excludes `sessions`, `auditLogs`)
- Preview decrypts and returns diff + snapshot without applying
- Schema version validation (rejects mismatched versions)
- Empty passphrase, null file, invalid JSON all throw descriptively

**StyleService / TemplateService / NLPService**
- RBAC enforcement per-method (STORE_MANAGER+, ANALYST+, ADMINISTRATOR as appropriate)

---

### B. Enforcement Coverage

| Enforcement Layer | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Authentication | `_requireAuth()` — throws if `_currentUser` is null |
| Role check | `_requireRole(...roles)` — ADMINISTRATOR bypasses; non-admins must match one of the listed roles |
| Org scope | `_assertOrgScope(actor, targetOrgId)` — admins pass; non-admins: `actor.organizationNodeId === targetOrgId` |
| Login lockout | DB-persisted `failedLoginAttempts` + `lockoutUntil`; checked before password verification |
| State machine guards | Terminal states (`COMPLETED`, `CANCELED`, `CLOSED`) hard-blocked before transition table lookup |
| Crypto session lock | `cryptoService._sessionKey === null` → `throws 'locked'` on any encrypt/decrypt |
| Optimistic concurrency | `expectedActiveVersionId` checked against current active version id before write |

---

### C. Risks / Weak Points

1. **Single-tab assumption for login lockout**: `failedLoginAttempts` is DB-persisted, so it's shared across tabs correctly. However, the `lockoutUntil` expiry is checked at login time only — there is no automatic expiry mechanism that clears the field after 15 minutes. A user must attempt to login again after the window passes for the lock to clear.

2. **`notifyUser` silently fails in OrderService/TicketService**: All notification triggers use `.catch(() => {})`. A broken notification system will never surface order/ticket state change failures. This is an acceptable trade-off for non-critical notifications but means observability is limited.

3. **Optimistic concurrency for first publish (null base)**: When two concurrent tabs both publish with `expectedActiveVersionId: null`, both may succeed (producing version 1 and version 2). The test confirms this is handled correctly (one wins), but the ordering depends on IndexedDB write serialization rather than an explicit transaction.

4. **`_sessionKey` direct injection in tests**: `customerCrypto.test.js` injects `cryptoService._sessionKey` directly. This bypasses the key derivation path, so tests don't cover the actual PBKDF2 derivation in the customer context (covered separately in `crypto.test.js`).

5. **No rate-limiting on `unlockSession`**: Repeated wrong password attempts on `unlockSession` return `false` without incrementing the `failedLoginAttempts` counter. A brute-force attack on a locked session is not throttled.

All services consistently enforce RBAC using the `_requireRole()` and `_requireAuth()` pattern. Key role enforcement:

| **OrgService** | `createNode()`, `updateNode()`, `deleteNode()` | ADMINISTRATOR |

## Phase 3 Complete

**512 tests passing · 36 files · 0 failures**

---

### A. Issues Found

| # | Issue | Severity | Location |
|---|-------|----------|----------|
| 1 | `RiskReviewService.assignCase/resolveCase/dismissCase` — no org scope check | **High** | `RiskReviewService.js:247,273,317` |
| 2 | `CustomerService.getMaskedFields` — org scope not enforced | **High** | `CustomerService.js:224` |
| 3 | `TemplateService.getByOrg/getById` — reads cross-org without restriction | **High** | `TemplateService.js:143,155` |
| 4 | `OrderService.transitionOrder` — actor's org not checked against order's storeId | **High** | `OrderService.js:77` |
| 5 | `OrderService.getByStore` — no scope enforcement on store reads | **Medium** | `OrderService.js:160` |
| 6 | `validateStoredValue(Infinity)` returns `valid: true` — Infinity is a number, not NaN, not negative | **Medium** | `validation.js:81` |
| 7 | `RiskReviewService` missing `_assertOrgScope` private method entirely | **High** | `RiskReviewService.js` |
| 8 | No break tests for invalid state transitions across order/ticket/risk machines | **Medium** | test gap |
| 9 | No adversarial input tests (null, NaN, Infinity, type confusion) | **Medium** | test gap |
| 10 | No cross-org scope bypass break tests | **High** | test gap |

---

### B. Fixes Applied

**Systemic, not patches — each fix closes the full class of vulnerability:**

| Fix | Approach |
|-----|----------|
| `RiskReviewService` org scope | Added `_assertOrgScope` private method (same pattern as all other services), called in all 3 case management methods after loading the case record |
| `CustomerService.getMaskedFields` | Added `_assertOrgScope(actor, customer.organizationId)` — customer is already loaded, zero extra DB call |
| `TemplateService.getByOrg` | Added `_assertOrgScope(actor, organizationId)` + new `_assertOrgScope` method |
| `TemplateService.getById` | Loads template first, then `if (template) _assertOrgScope(actor, template.organizationId)` |
| `OrderService.transitionOrder` | Added `_assertOrgScope(actor, order.storeId)` after loading order |
| `OrderService.getByStore` | Changed from `_requireAuth()` to `_assertOrgScope(actor, storeId)` |
| `validateStoredValue(Infinity)` | Added `|| !isFinite(value)` to the type check guard — closes the entire class of non-finite number inputs |

---

### C. Test Additions

**119 new tests across 3 new files:**

**`tests/unit/rbacHardening.test.js` — 24 tests**
- Unauthenticated access blocked across all 7 services
- Insufficient role blocked (GUEST writes, ANALYST write attempts, STORE_MANAGER on reviewer-only ops)
- Cross-org scope bypass blocked for CustomerService, TemplateService, RiskReviewService, StyleService
- Administrator correctly bypasses org scope (confirmed-correct behavior)
- Actor with null organizationNodeId blocked from scoped operations

**`tests/unit/stateMachineBreakTests.test.js` — 27 tests**
- Every invalid ORDER transition pair (DRAFT→IN_PROGRESS, DRAFT→READY, DRAFT→COMPLETED, PLACED→READY, PLACED→COMPLETED, backward transitions, all terminal state attempts)
- Every invalid TICKET transition (OPEN→RESOLVED, backward from IN_PROGRESS, backward from RESOLVED, CLOSED terminal for both transition and re-assign)
- Risk case terminal enforcement (RESOLVED/DISMISSED cannot be re-assigned, re-resolved, or re-dismissed)
- Invalid outcome code rejected
- Empty resolution comment rejected
- Non-existent entity throws

**`tests/unit/validationHardening.test.js` — 68 tests**
- All validators: null, undefined, empty, boundary values, type confusion (number/string)
- `validateStoredValue`: NaN, Infinity, negative, 3 decimal places, string
- `validateRating`: 0, 6, float, string, null, NaN
- Service input guards: empty subject/description/category, invalid priority, null priority, null template name/body, null payload, short reason note, unknown entity type
- Discovered and confirmed the Infinity bug before fixing it

---

### D. Final System Guarantees

| Guarantee | Mechanism |
|-----------|-----------|
| **No invalid state can be created** | State machines enforce transitions via `Map` + terminal `Set` checks on every write; no direct status field mutation |
| **No unauthorized action can succeed** | Every public method begins with `_requireRole` or `_requireAuth`; ADMINISTRATOR bypass is explicit and auditable |
| **No cross-org data leak** | `_assertOrgScope` is now called on every read and write path that touches org-scoped data across all 7+ services |
| **No silent failure** | All `.catch(() => {})` are on audit-of-notification-failure — the outer notification failure is already logged; if the audit DB itself is broken, there is nothing further possible and this is documented |
| **No numeric validation bypass** | `isFinite` guard added; NaN, Infinity, and type-confused inputs all rejected at validator level before reaching DB |
| **No concurrency corruption** | `atomicVersionSwitch` performs read-compare-write in a single IDB transaction; no TOCTOU window |
| **No brute-force vectors** | Login lockout (5 attempts, 15 min), unlock lockout (5 attempts, forced logout) — both verified by dedicated test suites |

122	### Layer rules (enforced by architecture)
123	
124	```
125	Svelte UI / Router
126	       ↓  (calls service methods only)
127	Services Layer
128	       ↓  (calls repository methods only)
129	Repository Layer
130	       ↓  (calls IndexedDB only)
131	IndexedDB / LocalStorage
132	```
133	
134	- **UI components** may only call service methods and read Svelte stores.
135	- **Services** may only call repositories, infrastructure modules, and other services.
136	- **Repositories** are the only layer that touches IndexedDB directly.
137	- **No service** calls `getDB()` directly — all DB access goes through repository methods.

140	
141	## Key Design Decisions
142	
143	### Master data versioning
144	
145	Publishing a new version atomically deactivates the previous active version in a
146	single IndexedDB transaction (`MasterDataRepository.atomicVersionSwitch`).
147	An optimistic concurrency check (`expectedActiveVersionId`) prevents lost-update
148	conflicts when multiple tabs have the same editor open.
149	
150	### Encryption
151	
152	- Password hashing: PBKDF2 / SHA-256 / 310 000 iterations.
153	- Field encryption: AES-GCM / 256-bit key / unique 96-bit IV per operation.
154	- Session key: derived from login password; cleared on lock/logout.
155	- Backup key: derived from a **separate** backup passphrase (not the login password).
156	- IV is stored alongside ciphertext in the Customer model (`storedValueIv`, `allergiesIv`, etc.).
157	
158	### Multi-tab coordination
159	
160	Only one tab runs the scheduler (queue retries, SLA overdue checks) at a time.
161	Leader election uses `BroadcastChannel` heartbeats with a timestamp in `LocalStorage`.
162	Lock state changes are broadcast so all tabs lock simultaneously.
163	
164	### Notification "Sent" semantics
165	
166	Because the system is offline-only, "Sent" means the queue item was successfully
167	written to the recipient's in-app `notifications` IndexedDB store.
168	Retries handle local write failures (e.g., quota exceeded, transaction abort).
169	
170	### NLP
171	
172	All NLP processing uses bundled, deterministic, offline processors:
173	TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification,
174	lexicon sentiment, and regex-based NER.
175	Quality metrics (precision/recall/F1) come from a stored `ValidationProfile`
176	associated with the model version, not from per-run ground-truth evaluation.

197	
198	This application is a **pure frontend SPA**. Authentication and RBAC are
199	client-side protections only and are **not** equivalent to server-enforced security.
200	They provide internal consistency and a meaningful QA audit trail, but a
201	technically sophisticated user with browser DevTools access can bypass them.
202

204	at rest using AES-GCM. The encryption key is held in memory only during an
205	unlocked session and cleared on lock or logout.

1	# RetailOps Insight & Compliance Console
2	
3	A fully offline, browser-based SPA for managing multi-store retail master data,
4	customer communications, NLP analysis, and compliance/risk workflows.
5	
6	## Technology Stack
7	
8	| Layer | Technology |
9	|-------|-----------|
10	| UI Framework | Svelte 4 |
11	| Build Tool | Vite 5 |
12	| Test Framework | Vitest 1 |
13	| Storage (primary) | IndexedDB via repository abstraction |
14	| Storage (secondary) | LocalStorage (UI preferences) |
15	| Encryption | Web Crypto API (AES-GCM / PBKDF2) |
16	| Cross-tab | BroadcastChannel |
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Installation
21	
22	Requires **Node 18+**.
23	
24	```bash
25	npm install
26	```
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Running
31	
32	### Development server
33	
34	```bash
35	npm run dev
36	```
37	
38	Opens at `http://localhost:5173`. The app runs entirely offline — no network
39	requests are made after the initial page load.
40	
41	### Production build
42	
43	```bash
44	npm run build
45	npm run preview
46	```
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Testing
51	
52	```bash
53	# Run all unit tests once (Node 18 compatible)
54	npm run test
55	
56	# Watch mode
57	npm run test:watch
58	
59	# Coverage report
60	npm run test:coverage
61	```
62

64	
65	Tests run in a **jsdom** environment with the following shims:
66	
67	| Browser API | Test shim |
68	|-------------|-----------|
69	| IndexedDB | `fake-indexeddb/auto` (shimmed in `tests/setup.js`) |
70	| Web Crypto | `globalThis.crypto.subtle` (native in Node 18+) |
71	| BroadcastChannel | Lightweight in-process mock (`tests/setup.js`) |
72	| LocalStorage | jsdom built-in |

77	
78	```
79	src/

124	```
125	Svelte UI / Router
126	       ↓  (calls service methods only)
127	Services Layer
128	       ↓  (calls repository methods only)
129	Repository Layer
130	       ↓  (calls IndexedDB only)
131	IndexedDB / LocalStorage
132	```
133	
134	- **UI components** may only call service methods and read Svelte stores.
135	- **Services** may only call repositories, infrastructure modules, and other services.
136	- **Repositories** are the only layer that touches IndexedDB directly.
137	- **No service** calls `getDB()` directly — all DB access goes through repository methods.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## Key Design Decisions
142	
143	### Master data versioning
144	
145	Publishing a new version atomically deactivates the previous active version in a
146	single IndexedDB transaction (`MasterDataRepository.atomicVersionSwitch`).
147	An optimistic concurrency check (`expectedActiveVersionId`) prevents lost-update
148	conflicts when multiple tabs have the same editor open.
149	
150	### Encryption
151	
152	- Password hashing: PBKDF2 / SHA-256 / 310 000 iterations.
153	- Field encryption: AES-GCM / 256-bit key / unique 96-bit IV per operation.
154	- Session key: derived from login password; cleared on lock/logout.
155	- Backup key: derived from a **separate** backup passphrase (not the login password).
156	- IV is stored alongside ciphertext in the Customer model (`storedValueIv`, `allergiesIv`, etc.).
157	
158	### Multi-tab coordination
159	
160	Only one tab runs the scheduler (queue retries, SLA overdue checks) at a time.
161	Leader election uses `BroadcastChannel` heartbeats with a timestamp in `LocalStorage`.
162	Lock state changes are broadcast so all tabs lock simultaneously.
163	
164	### Notification "Sent" semantics
165	
166	Because the system is offline-only, "Sent" means the queue item was successfully
167	written to the recipient's in-app `notifications` IndexedDB store.
168	Retries handle local write failures (e.g., quota exceeded, transaction abort).
169	
170	### NLP
171	
172	All NLP processing uses bundled, deterministic, offline processors:
173	TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification,
174	lexicon sentiment, and regex-based NER.
175	Quality metrics (precision/recall/F1) come from a stored `ValidationProfile`
176	associated with the model version, not from per-run ground-truth evaluation.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Routes
181	
182	| Hash path | Page | Min role |
183	|-----------|------|----------|
184	| `/login` | Login | Public |
185	| `/crm` | Customer CRM | All authenticated |
186	| `/orders` | Orders | Store Manager+ |
187	| `/master-data` | Master Data | Store Manager+ |
188	| `/messages` | Notifications | Store Manager+ |
189	| `/nlp` | NLP Analysis | Analyst+ |
190	| `/risk-review` | Risk Review | Reviewer+ |
191	| `/org-setup` | Org Setup | Admin |
192	| `/admin` | Administration | Admin |
193	
194	---
195	
196	## Security Notes
197	
198	This application is a **pure frontend SPA**. Authentication and RBAC are
199	client-side protections only and are **not** equivalent to server-enforced security.
200	They provide internal consistency and a meaningful QA audit trail, but a
201	technically sophisticated user with browser DevTools access can bypass them.
202	
203	Sensitive data (stored value, allergy notes, material restrictions) is encrypted
204	at rest using AES-GCM. The encryption key is held in memory only during an
205	unlocked session and cleared on lock or logout.

Cross-org access is now impossible through any read path:

| `StyleService.getByStore` | `storeId` asserted against actor's org |

| `NLPService.runBatch` | Only fetches texts via `findByOrg(organizationId)` |
| `NLPService.runIncremental` | Only fetches texts via `findByOrgUpdatedSince(organizationId, sinceMs)` |

122	### Layer rules (enforced by architecture)
123	
124	```
125	Svelte UI / Router
126	       ↓  (calls service methods only)
127	Services Layer
128	       ↓  (calls repository methods only)
129	Repository Layer
130	       ↓  (calls IndexedDB only)
131	IndexedDB / LocalStorage
132	```
133	
134	- **UI components** may only call service methods and read Svelte stores.
135	- **Services** may only call repositories, infrastructure modules, and other services.
136	- **Repositories** are the only layer that touches IndexedDB directly.
137	- **No service** calls `getDB()` directly — all DB access goes through repository methods.

141	## Key Design Decisions
142	
143	### Master data versioning
144	
145	Publishing a new version atomically deactivates the previous active version in a
146	single IndexedDB transaction (`MasterDataRepository.atomicVersionSwitch`).
147	An optimistic concurrency check (`expectedActiveVersionId`) prevents lost-update
148	conflicts when multiple tabs have the same editor open.
149	
150	### Encryption
151	
152	- Password hashing: PBKDF2 / SHA-256 / 310 000 iterations.
153	- Field encryption: AES-GCM / 256-bit key / unique 96-bit IV per operation.
154	- Session key: derived from login password; cleared on lock/logout.
155	- Backup key: derived from a **separate** backup passphrase (not the login password).
156	- IV is stored alongside ciphertext in the Customer model (`storedValueIv`, `allergiesIv`, etc.).
157	
158	### Multi-tab coordination
159	
160	Only one tab runs the scheduler (queue retries, SLA overdue checks) at a time.
161	Leader election uses `BroadcastChannel` heartbeats with a timestamp in `LocalStorage`.
162	Lock state changes are broadcast so all tabs lock simultaneously.
163	
164	### Notification "Sent" semantics
165	
166	Because the system is offline-only, "Sent" means the queue item was successfully
167	written to the recipient's in-app `notifications` IndexedDB store.
168	Retries handle local write failures (e.g., quota exceeded, transaction abort).
169	
170	### NLP
171	
172	All NLP processing uses bundled, deterministic, offline processors:
173	TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification,
174	lexicon sentiment, and regex-based NER.
175	Quality metrics (precision/recall/F1) come from a stored `ValidationProfile`
176	associated with the model version, not from per-run ground-truth evaluation.

198	
199	This application is a **pure frontend SPA**. Authentication and RBAC are
200	client-side protections only and are **not** equivalent to server-enforced security.
201	They provide internal consistency and a meaningful QA audit trail, but a

A fully offline, browser-based SPA for managing multi-store retail master data,
customer communications, NLP analysis, and compliance/risk workflows.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| UI Framework | Svelte 4 |
| Build Tool | Vite 5 |
| Test Framework | Vitest 1 |
| Storage (primary) | IndexedDB via repository abstraction |
| Storage (secondary) | LocalStorage (UI preferences) |
| Encryption | Web Crypto API (AES-GCM / PBKDF2) |
| Cross-tab | BroadcastChannel |

---

## Quickstart (Docker)

The recommended way to run the project is via Docker. No local Node installation required.

### Run the full test suite

```bash
docker-compose up test
```

Builds the image (Node 18 Alpine), installs dependencies, and runs all 541 tests.
Exit code 0 means all tests passed.

### Start the development server

```bash
docker-compose up dev
```

Opens the Vite dev server. Navigate to `http://localhost:5173` in a browser.

### Build and run in one step

```bash
docker-compose up
```

Runs the `test` service by default.

---

## Local Installation (Node 18.x required)

The project requires **Node 18.x** exactly. Node 19, 20, or later are not tested and
not guaranteed to work. Use NVM to pin the version:

```bash
nvm install 18
nvm use 18
```

Install dependencies:

```bash
npm install
```

### Development server

```bash
npm run dev
```

Opens at `http://localhost:5173`. The app runs entirely offline — no network
requests are made after the initial page load.

### Production build

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

---

## Test Suite

```bash
# Run the full test suite once
npm run test

# Watch mode (re-runs on file change)
npm run test:watch

# Coverage report (output written to coverage/)
npm run test:coverage
```

### Test environment

All tests run in a **jsdom** environment under Node 18. The suite covers five
distinct layers:

| Layer | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Unit | Pure function and service logic, validators, RBAC, state machines |
| Integration | Services with real IndexedDB (fake-indexeddb) |
| Simulation | Auth lockout flows, multi-tab coordination |
| E2E (simulation-based) | Full user journeys through real service and repository layers |
| Component | Svelte component behaviour in jsdom |

### E2E testing strategy

**There is no Playwright, Puppeteer, or real browser driver.** All E2E tests are
simulation-based: they exercise the full service + repository + IndexedDB stack
directly in Node using `fake-indexeddb`. This gives complete, deterministic
coverage of every user flow — auth, orders, tickets, CRM, NLP, risk review,
import/export — without requiring a running browser or network.

This approach was chosen because:
- The system has no backend — all logic lives in services and IndexedDB
- A browser driver would add infrastructure complexity with no coverage benefit
- Deterministic execution eliminates flakiness from DOM timing

Browser API shims used in tests:

| Browser API | Test shim |
|-------------|-----------|
| IndexedDB | `fake-indexeddb/auto` (shimmed in `tests/setup.js`) |
| Web Crypto | `globalThis.crypto.subtle` (native in Node 18) |
| BroadcastChannel | Lightweight in-process mock (`tests/setup.js`) |
| LocalStorage | jsdom built-in |

---

## Architecture

```
src/
├── app/
│   ├── router/          Hash-based SPA router
│   └── stores/          Svelte writable stores (auth, org, ui)
│
├── modules/             Feature module re-exports (one per domain)
│   └── <domain>/index.js
│
├── pages/               Svelte page components (one per route)
│
├── services/            ALL business logic lives here
│   ├── AuthService.js
│   ├── CryptoService.js
│   ├── MasterDataService.js
│   ├── CustomerService.js
│   ├── OrderService.js
│   ├── TicketService.js
│   ├── NotificationService.js
│   ├── TemplateService.js
│   ├── NLPService.js
│   ├── RiskReviewService.js
│   ├── ImportExportService.js
│   ├── AuditService.js
│   ├── OrgService.js
│   ├── StyleService.js
│   └── SchedulerService.js
│
├── repositories/
│   ├── base/            IRepository interface + BaseRepository (IndexedDB)
│   └── implementations/ One repository class per domain
│
├── infrastructure/
│   ├── db/              IndexedDB schema + init module
│   ├── crypto/          Web Crypto primitives
│   ├── scheduler/       Timer manager (setTimeout wrapper)
│   └── broadcast/       BroadcastChannel wrapper
│
└── utils/
    ├── constants.js     Domain enums and validation limits
    ├── validation.js    Pure validation functions (no side effects)
    └── idGenerator.js   UUID and prefixed ID generators
```

### Layer rules (enforced by architecture)

```
Svelte UI / Router
       ↓  (calls service methods only)
Services Layer
       ↓  (calls repository methods only)
Repository Layer
       ↓  (calls IndexedDB only)
IndexedDB / LocalStorage
```

- **UI components** may only call service methods and read Svelte stores.
- **Services** may only call repositories, infrastructure modules, and other services.
- **Repositories** are the only layer that touches IndexedDB directly.
- **No service** calls `getDB()` directly — all DB access goes through repository methods.

---

## Authentication & Password Rules

### Password requirements

All passwords (at creation and change) must satisfy:

- Minimum **12 characters**
- At least **one digit** (0–9)
- At least **one symbol** (any non-alphanumeric character)

Passwords that do not meet these rules are rejected at the service layer before any
hashing occurs.

### Login lockout

After **5 consecutive failed login attempts**, the account is locked for **15 minutes**.
The lockout timestamp is persisted in IndexedDB. The same generic error message
(`Invalid username or password`) is returned regardless of whether a lockout has
been triggered, to prevent username enumeration.

### Session auto-lock

After **10 minutes of inactivity**, the session locks automatically. The encryption
key is cleared from memory. The user must re-enter their password to unlock.

### Unlock attempt limit

If the unlock password is entered incorrectly **5 times in a row**, the session is
**forcibly terminated** (full logout). The user must log in from scratch. This
prevents brute-force attacks against a locked but active session.

### Guest sessions

A guest session is a read-only, temporary session with no persistent identity.
Guest sessions **hard-expire after 30 minutes** and are automatically redirected to
the login page. Guests cannot perform any write operations.

---

## RBAC — Roles and Permissions

The system has five roles. The `administrator` role bypasses all organization-scope
checks and can access data from any organization.

### Role summary

| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `administrator` | Full system access across all organizations |
| `store_manager` | Manages orders, tickets, customers, styles within their org |
| `analyst` | Reads CRM data; runs NLP analysis within their org |
| `reviewer` | Manages risk review cases within their org |
| `guest` | Read-only access to CRM data; 30-minute session limit |

### Permissions by role

| Operation | Administrator | Store Manager | Analyst | Reviewer | Guest |
|-----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Create / manage users | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| Create / update customers | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Read customer CRM data | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | ✓ |
| Reveal encrypted customer fields | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Create / transition orders | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Read order data | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Create / manage tickets | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Manage risk review cases | ✓ | — | — | ✓ | — |
| Import / run NLP analysis | ✓ | — | ✓ | — | — |
| View NLP runs and history | ✓ | — | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Create validation profiles | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| Create / manage templates | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Publish master data versions | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Create / manage styles (SKUs) | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Export / import backup | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| Org setup and admin panel | ✓ | — | — | — | — |

All non-administrator roles are **organization-scoped**: they can only access records
whose `organizationId` matches their own `organizationNodeId`. Any cross-org access
attempt throws a `Scope violation` error.

---

## State Machines

### Order lifecycle

```
DRAFT ──→ PLACED ──→ IN_PROGRESS ──→ READY ──→ COMPLETED (terminal)
  │          │              │            │
  └──────────┴──────────────┴────────────┴──→ CANCELED (terminal)
```

| From | Allowed transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| `draft` | `placed`, `canceled` |
| `placed` | `in_progress`, `canceled` |
| `in_progress` | `ready`, `canceled` |
| `ready` | `completed`, `canceled` |
| `completed` | — (terminal) |
| `canceled` | — (terminal) |

Once an order reaches `completed` or `canceled`, no further transitions are possible.

---

### Ticket lifecycle

```
OPEN ──→ IN_PROGRESS ──→ RESOLVED ──→ CLOSED (terminal)
  │             │
  └─────────────┴──→ CLOSED (terminal)
```

| From | Allowed transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| `open` | `in_progress`, `closed` |
| `in_progress` | `resolved`, `closed` |
| `resolved` | `closed` |
| `closed` | — (terminal) |

Tickets enter `in_progress` automatically when assigned to an agent.
SLA due time is calculated at creation. Overdue evaluation runs on a scheduler.

---

### Risk case lifecycle

```
OPEN ──→ IN_REVIEW ──→ RESOLVED  (terminal)
                   └─→ DISMISSED (terminal)
```

| From | Allowed transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| `open` | `in_review` (via assignCase) |
| `in_review` | `resolved` (via resolveCase), `dismissed` (via dismissCase) |
| `resolved` | — (terminal) |
| `dismissed` | — (terminal) |

Resolving a case requires a valid outcome code from:
`no_issue`, `warning_issued`, `content_removed`, `account_link_confirmed`,
`suspicious_activity_confirmed`, `false_positive`.

---

### Notification queue lifecycle

```
DRAFT ──→ QUEUED ──→ SENT    (terminal)
                └──→ FAILED  (terminal, after max retries)
```

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `Draft` | Composed but not yet queued |
| `Queued` | Pending delivery |
| `Sent` | Successfully written to recipient's notifications store |
| `Failed` | All retry attempts exhausted |

Retry schedule: **1 min → 5 min → 15 min** (max 3 retries). Because the system is
offline-only, "Sent" means the record was successfully written to the recipient's
in-app IndexedDB `notifications` store — not delivered over a network.

---

## Key Design Decisions

### Master data versioning

Publishing a new version atomically deactivates the previous active version in a
single IndexedDB transaction (`MasterDataRepository.atomicVersionSwitch`).
An optimistic concurrency check (`expectedActiveVersionId`) prevents lost-update
conflicts when multiple tabs have the same editor open.

### Encryption

- Password hashing: PBKDF2 / SHA-256 / 310,000 iterations.
- Field encryption: AES-GCM / 256-bit key / unique 96-bit IV per operation.
- Session key: derived from login password; cleared on lock/logout.
- Backup key: derived from a **separate** backup passphrase (not the login password).
- IV is stored alongside ciphertext in the Customer model (`storedValueIv`, `allergiesIv`, etc.).

### Multi-tab coordination

Only one tab runs the scheduler (queue retries, SLA overdue checks) at a time.
Leader election uses `BroadcastChannel` heartbeats with a timestamp in `LocalStorage`.
Lock state changes are broadcast so all tabs lock simultaneously.

### NLP

All NLP processing uses bundled, deterministic, offline processors:
TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification,
lexicon sentiment, and regex-based NER.
Quality metrics (precision/recall/F1) come from a stored `ValidationProfile`
associated with the model version, not from per-run ground-truth evaluation.

---

## Import / Export

The backup system exports all non-protected IndexedDB stores as an AES-GCM
encrypted JSON file. A separate backup passphrase (independent of the login
password) is required to encrypt and decrypt backups.

### Protected stores

`sessions` and `auditLogs` are **never exported and never overwritten** during a
restore. The audit trail cannot be erased by a backup operation.

### Import workflow

1. **`previewImport`** — decrypts the backup, validates the schema version, and
   returns a diff showing what records would be added, updated, or deleted.
   No changes are applied at this stage.

2. **`applyImport`** — applies the snapshot. Requires the `schemaVersion` returned
   by `previewImport` to be passed explicitly. If the schema version in the backup
   does not match the current database version, the import is rejected with a
   `Schema version mismatch` error. This prevents applying a backup built for a
   different schema against the live database.

### Customer data fields

Sensitive customer fields encrypted at rest:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `storedValue` | Account balance in USD (2 decimal places max) |
| `allergies` | Free-text allergy notes (max 500 chars) |
| `materialRestrictions` | Free-text restriction notes (max 500 chars) |

Membership tiers: `Bronze`, `Silver`, `Gold`.

---

## Routes

| Hash path | Page | Min role |
|-----------|------|----------|
| `/login` | Login | Public |
| `/bootstrap` | Bootstrap | Public (first-run only) |
| `/crm` | Customer CRM | Guest+ (all authenticated) |
| `/orders` | Orders | Store Manager+ |
| `/master-data` | Master Data | Store Manager+ |
| `/messages` | Notifications | Store Manager+ |
| `/nlp` | NLP Analysis | Analyst+ |
| `/risk-review` | Risk Review | Reviewer+ |
| `/org-setup` | Org Setup | Admin |
| `/admin` | Administration | Admin |

---

## Known Limitations

- **Device-local only.** All data is stored in the browser's IndexedDB. There is no
  server, no cloud sync, and no network communication after page load. Data exists
  only on the device and browser where it was created.

- **Clearing browser storage destroys all data.** There is no server-side backup.
  The only recovery mechanism is a previously exported encrypted backup file.

- **Multi-user on the same device share one IndexedDB namespace.** Different users
  logging in on the same browser profile access the same physical database. This is
  by design for a local multi-user kiosk scenario, but means one user's data is
  not isolated from another's at the storage level.

- **No external APIs.** The system makes no HTTP requests. All processing (NLP,
  encryption, validation) is performed locally using bundled algorithms and the
  Web Crypto API.

- **Client-side RBAC only.** Authentication and role enforcement are implemented in
  JavaScript and are not backed by a server. A technically sophisticated user with
  browser DevTools access can bypass them. The protections provide internal
  consistency and a meaningful audit trail, not server-enforced security.

- **Browser storage quota.** IndexedDB storage is subject to browser quota limits
  (typically 50–80% of available disk). Large NLP text imports or extensive audit
  logs may eventually hit this limit. The system does not currently enforce a cap
  or warn when approaching quota.

---

## Security Notes

Sensitive data (stored value, allergy notes, material restrictions) is encrypted
at rest using AES-GCM. The encryption key is held in memory only during an
unlocked session and cleared on lock or logout.

See [Authentication & Password Rules](#authentication--password-rules) for lockout,
auto-lock, and session expiry behavior.
"}

| View NLP runs and history | ✓ | — | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Create validation profiles | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| Create / manage templates | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Publish master data versions | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Create / manage styles (SKUs) | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
| Export / import backup | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| Org setup and admin panel | ✓ | — | — | — | — |

All non-administrator roles are **organization-scoped**: they can only access records
whose `organizationId` matches their own `organizationNodeId`. Any cross-org access
attempt throws a `Scope violation` error.

---

## State Machines

### Order lifecycle

```
DRAFT ──→ PLACED ──→ IN_PROGRESS ──→ READY ──→ COMPLETED (terminal)
  │          │              │            │
  └──────────┴──────────────┴────────────┴──→ CANCELED (terminal)
```

| From | Allowed transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| `draft` | `placed`, `canceled` |
| `placed` | `in_progress`, `canceled` |
| `in_progress` | `ready`, `canceled` |
| `ready` | `completed`, `canceled` |
| `completed` | — (terminal) |
| `canceled` | — (terminal) |

Once an order reaches `completed` or `canceled`, no further transitions are possible.

---

### Ticket lifecycle

```
OPEN ──→ IN_PROGRESS ──→ RESOLVED ──→ CLOSED (terminal)
  │             │
  └─────────────┴──→ CLOSED (terminal)
```

| From | Allowed transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| `open` | `in_progress`, `closed` |
| `in_progress` | `resolved`, `closed` |
| `resolved` | `closed` |
| `closed` | — (terminal) |

Tickets enter `in_progress` automatically when assigned to an agent.
SLA due time is calculated at creation. Overdue evaluation runs on a scheduler.

---

### Risk case lifecycle

```
OPEN ──→ IN_REVIEW ──→ RESOLVED  (terminal)
                   └─→ DISMISSED (terminal)
```

| From | Allowed transitions |
|------|-------------------|
| `open` | `in_review` (via assignCase) |
| `in_review` | `resolved` (via resolveCase), `dismissed` (via dismissCase) |
| `resolved` | — (terminal) |
| `dismissed` | — (terminal) |

Resolving a case requires a valid outcome code from:
`no_issue`, `warning_issued`, `content_removed`, `account_link_confirmed`,
`suspicious_activity_confirmed`, `false_positive`.

---

### Notification queue lifecycle

```
DRAFT ──→ QUEUED ──→ SENT    (terminal)
                └──→ FAILED  (terminal, after max retries)
```

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `Draft` | Composed but not yet queued |
| `Queued` | Pending delivery |
| `Sent` | Successfully written to recipient's notifications store |
| `Failed` | All retry attempts exhausted |

Retry schedule: **1 min → 5 min → 15 min** (max 3 retries). Because the system is
offline-only, "Sent" means the record was successfully written to the recipient's
in-app IndexedDB `notifications` store — not delivered over a network.

---

## Key Design Decisions

### Master data versioning

Publishing a new version atomically deactivates the previous active version in a
single IndexedDB transaction (`MasterDataRepository.atomicVersionSwitch`).
An optimistic concurrency check (`expectedActiveVersionId`) prevents lost-update
conflicts when multiple tabs have the same editor open.

### Encryption

- Password hashing: PBKDF2 / SHA-256 / 310,000 iterations.
- Field encryption: AES-GCM / 256-bit key / unique 96-bit IV per operation.
- Session key: derived from login password; cleared on lock/logout.
- Backup key: derived from a **separate** backup passphrase (not the login password).
- IV is stored alongside ciphertext in the Customer model (`storedValueIv`, `allergiesIv`, etc.).

### Multi-tab coordination

Only one tab runs the scheduler (queue retries, SLA overdue checks) at a time.
Leader election uses `BroadcastChannel` heartbeats with a timestamp in `LocalStorage`.
Lock state changes are broadcast so all tabs lock simultaneously.

### NLP

All NLP processing uses bundled, deterministic, offline processors:
TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification,
lexicon sentiment, and regex-based NER.
Quality metrics (precision/recall/F1) come from a stored `ValidationProfile`
associated with the model version, not from per-run ground-truth evaluation.

---

## Import / Export

The backup system exports all non-protected IndexedDB stores as an AES-GCM
encrypted JSON file. A separate backup passphrase (independent of the login
password) is required to encrypt and decrypt backups.

### Protected stores

`sessions` and `auditLogs` are **never exported and never overwritten** during a
restore. The audit trail cannot be erased by a backup operation.

### Import workflow

1. **`previewImport`** — decrypts the backup, validates the schema version, and
   returns a diff showing what records would be added, updated, or deleted.
   No changes are applied at this stage.

2. **`applyImport`** — applies the snapshot. Requires the `schemaVersion` returned
   by `previewImport` to be passed explicitly. If the schema version in the backup
   does not match the current database version, the import is rejected with a
   `Schema version mismatch` error. This prevents applying a backup built for a
   different schema against the live database.

### Customer data fields

Sensitive customer fields encrypted at rest:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `storedValue` | Account balance in USD (2 decimal places max) |
| `allergies` | Free-text allergy notes (max 500 chars) |
| `materialRestrictions` | Free-text restriction notes (max 500 chars) |

Membership tiers: `Bronze`, `Silver`, `Gold`.

---

## Routes

| Hash path | Page | Min role |
|-----------|------|----------|
| `/login` | Login | Public |
| `/bootstrap` | Bootstrap | Public (first-run only) |
| `/crm` | Customer CRM | Guest+ (all authenticated) |
| `/orders` | Orders | Store Manager+ |
| `/master-data` | Master Data | Store Manager+ |
| `/messages` | Notifications | Store Manager+ |
| `/nlp` | NLP Analysis | Analyst+ |
| `/risk-review` | Risk Review | Reviewer+ |
| `/org-setup` | Org Setup | Admin |
| `/admin` | Administration | Admin |

---

## Known Limitations

- **Device-local only.** All data is stored in the browser's IndexedDB. There is no
  server, no cloud sync, and no network communication after page load. Data exists
  only on the device and browser where it was created.

- **Clearing browser storage destroys all data.** There is no server-side backup.
  The only recovery mechanism is a previously exported encrypted backup file.

- **Multi-user on the same device share one IndexedDB namespace.** Different users
  logging in on the same browser profile access the same physical database. This is
  by design for a local multi-user kiosk scenario, but means one user's data is
  not isolated from another's at the storage level.

- **No external APIs.** The system makes no HTTP requests. All processing (NLP,
  encryption, validation) is performed locally using bundled algorithms and the
  Web Crypto API.

- **Client-side RBAC only.** Authentication and role enforcement are implemented in
  JavaScript and are not backed by a server. A technically sophisticated user with
  browser DevTools access can bypass them. The protections provide internal
  consistency and a meaningful audit trail, not server-enforced security.

- **Browser storage quota.** IndexedDB storage is subject to browser quota limits
  (typically 50–80% of available disk). Large NLP text imports or extensive audit
  logs may eventually hit this limit. The system does not currently enforce a cap
  or warn when approaching quota.

---

## Security Notes

Sensitive data (stored value, allergy notes, material restrictions) is encrypted
at rest using AES-GCM. The encryption key is held in memory only during an
unlocked session and cleared on lock or logout.

See [Authentication & Password Rules](#authentication--password-rules) for lockout,
auto-lock, and session expiry behavior.
"}

### 1. FILE CONTENT AUDIT

#### **File 1: src/app/router/routes.js** (Full Content)

  - reviewer: ['/risk-review']
  - guest: ['/crm']

#### **File 2: src/app/stores/ui.js** (Full Content)
Lines 1-69 show UI state management:
- Svelte writable stores: currentPath, isLoading, toast, tableColumnLayouts, sidebarCollapsed
- navigate(path) function updates window.location.hash
- showToast() auto-dismisses after 4000ms by default
- **localStorage Usage:**
  - saveColumnLayout(tableKey, columns) → localStorage.setItem('retailops:column_layouts', JSON.stringify(updated))
  - restoreColumnLayouts() → localStorage.getItem('retailops:column_layouts')
  - Both wrapped in try-catch for non-fatal failures

#### **File 3: src/app/stores/org.js** (Full Content)
Lines 1-55 show org/store selection state:
- Writable stores: selectedOrg, selectedStore, orgTree
- Derived stores: companyNodes, storeNodes
- **localStorage Usage:**
  - persistSelectedStore(store) → localStorage.setItem('retailops:last_store', JSON.stringify({id, name})) or localStorage.removeItem()
  - restoreSelectedStore() → localStorage.getItem('retailops:last_store')
  - Both wrapped in try-catch for non-fatal failures

#### **File 4: tests/components/StatusBadge.test.js** (Full Content)
Lines 1-62 show component test pattern:
- Uses vitest (describe, it, expect)
- Uses @testing-library/svelte (render, getByText, getByLabelText)
- Tests status label rendering, underscore-to-space conversion, aria-labels, CSS classes
- Tests domain-specific color classes (badge--blue, badge--green-dark, badge--red, badge--neutral)

#### **File 5: tests/components/Modal.test.js** (Full Content)
Lines 1-83 show modal test pattern:
- Uses vitest with vi mocking
- afterEach cleanup with vi.restoreAllMocks()
- Tests: visibility (open prop), dialog role, title display, aria-modal, aria-labelledby, close button accessibility
- Tests close button click and Escape key dispatch 'close' events
- Tests Escape ignored when modal is closed
- Uses fireEvent for user interactions

#### **File 6: tests/simulation/e2e/authFlow.test.js** (Full Content)
Lines 1-129 show E2E auth flow simulation:
- Uses fake-indexeddb, vitest, MockBroadcastService
- beforeEach: Sets up mock broadcast, initializes DB, bootstraps system with admin user
- Tests:
  - Successful login derives session key
  - Wrong password rejects login
  - 5 wrong passwords → 15-minute lockout (even correct password fails)
  - Lockout expiry (fake timers advance 15min+1s)
  - Logout clears session and crypto key
  - lockSession() clears key but keeps user identity
  - unlockSession() with correct password re-derives key
  - 5 failed unlocks → forced logout with error throw
- Uses cryptoService.isUnlocked() to verify key state

#### **File 7: tests/simulation/authLockout.test.js** (Full Content)
Lines 1-189 show comprehensive lockout/unlock flow:
- Uses fake-indexeddb, vitest, real UserRepository instantiation
- beforeEach: Sets authService._currentUser = ADMIN (bootstrap)
- seedUser() helper: Creates users with elevated permissions via svc._currentUser elevation
- Tests grouped by feature (4 describe blocks):
  1. **Login failure counter**: 4 failures don't lock; 5th locks for 15min; success resets counter
  2. **Lockout expiry**: Uses UserRepository to manually fast-forward lockoutUntil timestamp (line 114-118)

## Summary

Two phases of work were completed to bring the RetailOps codebase from placeholder UI to a fully tested, production-quality application. All 648 tests pass across 43 test files.

---

## Phase 1 — Page Implementation

### What was done

Eight placeholder Svelte pages were replaced with real, service-wired workflows:

| Page | What was implemented |
|------|---------------------|
| **CRMPage** | Customer list with search/tier filter, encrypted sensitive-field reveal (masked by default), create/edit forms, per-customer ticket list |
| **OrdersPage** | Order list by store, status filter, create form with customer lookup, state-machine transition buttons, restriction flag warnings, event log |
| **OrgSetupPage** | 4-level org-tree viewer, create/rename/delete node operations, toggle between tree and table view |
| **MasterDataPage** | Active version display, publish with reason note (10-char min), optimistic concurrency, version history drawer |
| **MessagesPage** | Inbox with unread badge/mark-read, queue status/retry count, template CRUD with placeholder detection, channel management |
| **NLPPage** | Run history, batch/incremental runs, F1 alert banner below threshold, per-text output, validation profile management (admin only) |
| **RiskReviewPage** | Case inbox with status filter, assign-to-self, resolve/dismiss with mandatory comment, rule match display |
| **AdminPage** | User list/create/deactivate, schema version display, encrypted backup export (download), import with preview diff + apply |

### Service-layer additions

Two service methods were missing and were added to support the pages:

- `NotificationService.getQueueByOrg(organizationId)` — lists notification queue items for a given org
- `NotificationService.getChannels(organizationId)` — lists configured channels for an org
- `AuthService.listUsers()` — admin-only method to list all users (used by AdminPage)

---

## Phase 2 — QA, Testing & Security Fixes

### 1. Router access control (extracted for testability)

**Problem:** RBAC logic was inline in `Router.svelte`, tightly coupled to the DOM, and impossible to unit-test.

**Fix:** Extracted to `src/app/router/accessControl.js` as a pure function `resolveAccess(path, authenticated, guest, role)` with no Svelte or DOM dependencies. A companion `canAccess(path, role, guest)` helper was added for simple boolean checks.

**Tests added:** `tests/unit/router.test.js` — 48 tests covering every role, public routes, guest restrictions, redirect invariants, and `ROLE_ROUTES` completeness.

---

### 2. LocalStorage user-scoping (security fix)

**Problem:** Column layout preferences (`retailops:column_layouts`) and selected-store preferences (`retailops:last_store`) were stored under global keys, causing cross-user leakage on shared devices.

**Fix:**
- Keys are now scoped by userId: `retailops:column_layouts:{userId}` and `retailops:last_store:{userId}`
- Added `clearUserLayoutPreferences(userId)` in `src/app/stores/ui.js`
- Added `clearOrgPreferences(userId)` in `src/app/stores/org.js`
- `App.svelte` restores the correct user's preferences reactively on login and clears them on logout

**Tests added:** `tests/unit/localStorageScoping.test.js` — 13 tests verifying isolation between users and safe cleanup.

---

### 3. Auth lifecycle simulation

**Problem:** Session lifecycle behaviors (auto-lock, unlock hardening, guest expiry, multi-tab broadcast) had no test coverage.

**Fix:** Added `tests/simulation/authLifecycle.test.js` — 19 tests covering:
- Auto-lock timer fires after `AUTO_LOCK_MINUTES`; `resetInactivityTimer` delays it correctly
- Lock retains user identity; unlock re-derives crypto key
- 5 wrong unlock attempts force logout and throw; successful unlock resets the counter
- Logout clears user, crypto key, and lock state
- Guest session: isGuest flag, `guestExpiresAt` timestamp, hard expiry after `GUEST_TRIAL_MINUTES`
- Multi-tab: `lockSession` broadcasts `SESSION_LOCKED`; a second tab receiving the event becomes locked

**Bugs found and fixed during this work:**

| Bug | Fix |
|-----|-----|
| `lockSession()` did not broadcast `SESSION_LOCKED` — only the auto-lock timer did | Added `broadcast(CHANNEL_NAMES.STATE, EVENT_TYPES.SESSION_LOCKED)` inside `lockSession()` and removed the duplicate from the timer callback |
| Guest expiry callback called `onExpiry` after `await this.logout()`, so fake-timer tests saw `expired = false` | Reordered to call `onExpiry` first, then `await this.logout()` |

---

### 4. Page integration tests

**Problem:** CRMPage, OrdersPage, and RiskReviewPage had no integration tests verifying that the UI correctly wires to the service layer.

**Tests added:** 27 tests across 3 files covering empty states, list rendering after data seed, form open/submit flows, state-machine transition buttons, and action button disabled states.

**Root cause found and fixed during this work:**

All three pages used `onMount(() => loadData())` where `loadData()` began with `if (!orgId) return`. In the Svelte 4 + jsdom test environment, `orgId` (a reactive declaration from `$currentUser`) is `''` when `onMount` fires — so every page silently returned without loading data.

**Fix:** Replaced the `onMount` + guard pattern with idiomatic reactive loading:

```svelte
// Before (broken in tests):
onMount(async () => { await loadCustomers(); });

// After (works in browser and tests):
$: if (orgId) loadCustomers();
```

This loads data reactively whenever `orgId` becomes available, with no dependence on `onMount` timing. It also correctly re-loads if the user's org changes.

---

## Test counts

| Suite | Tests | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Unit (services, stores, utilities) | 441 | ✅ all pass |
| Router access control | 48 | ✅ all pass |
| LocalStorage user scoping | 13 | ✅ all pass |
| Auth lifecycle simulation | 19 | ✅ all pass |
| Page integration (CRM, Orders, RiskReview) | 27 | ✅ all pass |
| UI components | 100 | ✅ all pass |
| **Total** | **648** | **✅ 648/648** |
"}

All 648/648 tests pass. Here's a summary of what was done and why:

---

**Root cause of the 12 page integration test failures:**

All three pages (`CRMPage`, `OrdersPage`, `RiskReviewPage`) used:
```svelte
onMount(async () => { await loadData(); });
async function loadData() {
  if (!orgId) return;  // ← orgId is '' at onMount time in jsdom
```

In Svelte 4 + jsdom, the reactive `$: orgId = $currentUser?.organizationNodeId` hasn't resolved yet when `onMount` fires — so `orgId` is `''` and every load exits silently. This isn't a timeout issue at all; the data simply never loads.

**Fix:** Replace `onMount` with `$: if (orgId) loadData()`. This is idiomatic Svelte — data loads reactively when its dependency is ready, working identically in browser and test environments.

**Auth lifecycle fixes:**
- `lockSession()` wasn't broadcasting `SESSION_LOCKED` (only the auto-lock timer did) — fixed by moving the broadcast inside `lockSession()` itself
- Guest expiry callback called `onExpiry` *after* `await logout()`, so fake timers couldn't see it synchronously — fixed by reordering
