content.text: Now let me read the README and the specific pages I need to fix:

1	# RetailOps Insight & Compliance Console
2	
3	A fully offline, browser-based SPA for managing multi-store retail master data,
4	customer communications, NLP analysis, and compliance/risk workflows.
5	
6	## Technology Stack
7	
8	| Layer | Technology |
9	|-------|-----------|
10	| UI Framework | Svelte 4 |
11	| Build Tool | Vite 5 |
12	| Test Framework | Vitest 1 |
13	| Storage (primary) | IndexedDB via repository abstraction |
14	| Storage (secondary) | LocalStorage (UI preferences) |
15	| Encryption | Web Crypto API (AES-GCM / PBKDF2) |
16	| Cross-tab | BroadcastChannel |
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Quickstart (Docker)
21	
22	The recommended way to run the project is via Docker. No local Node installation required.
23	
24	### Run the full test suite
25	
26	```bash
27	docker-compose up test
28	```
29	
30	Builds the image (Node 18 Alpine), installs dependencies, and runs all 541 tests.
31	Exit code 0 means all tests passed.
32	
33	### Start the development server
34	
35	```bash
36	docker-compose up dev
37	```
38	
39	Opens the Vite dev server. Navigate to `http://localhost:5173` in a browser.
40	
41	### Build and run in one step
42	
43	```bash
44	docker-compose up
45	```
46	
47	Runs the `test` service by default.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Local Installation (Node 18.x required)
52	
53	The project requires **Node 18.x** exactly. Node 19, 20, or later are not tested and
54	not guaranteed to work. Use NVM to pin the version:
55	
56	```bash
57	nvm install 18
58	nvm use 18
59	```
60

60	
61	Install dependencies:
62	
63	```bash
64	npm install
65	```
66	
67	### Development server
68	
69	```bash
70	npm run dev
71	```
72	
73	Opens at `http://localhost:5173`. The app runs entirely offline — no network
74	requests are made after the initial page load.
75	
76	### Production build
77	
78	```bash
79	npm run build
80	npm run preview
81	```
82	
83	---
84	
85	## Test Suite
86	
87	```bash
88	# Run the full test suite once
89	npm run test
90	
91	# Watch mode (re-runs on file change)
92	npm run test:watch
93	
94	# Coverage report (output written to coverage/)
95	npm run test:coverage
96	```
97	
98	### Test environment
99	
100	All tests run in a **jsdom** environment under Node 18. The suite covers five
101	distinct layers:
102	
103	| Layer | Description |
104	|-------|-------------|
105	| Unit | Pure function and service logic, validators, RBAC, state machines |
106	| Integration | Services with real IndexedDB (fake-indexeddb) |
107	| Simulation | Auth lockout flows, multi-tab coordination |
108	| E2E (simulation-based) | Full user journeys through real service and repository layers |
109	| Component | Svelte component behaviour in jsdom |
110	
111	### E2E testing strategy
112	
113	**There is no Playwright, Puppeteer, or real browser driver.** All E2E tests are
114	simulation-based: they exercise the full service + repository + IndexedDB stack
115	directly in Node using `fake-indexeddb`. This gives complete, deterministic
116	coverage of every user flow — auth, orders, tickets, CRM, NLP, risk review,
117	import/export — without requiring a running browser or network.
118	
119	This approach was chosen because:
120	- The system has no backend — all logic lives in services and IndexedDB
121	- A browser driver would add infrastructure complexity with no coverage benefit
122	- Deterministic execution eliminates flakiness from DOM timing
123	
124	Browser API shims used in tests:
125	
126	| Browser API | Test shim |
127	|-------------|-----------|
128	| IndexedDB | `fake-indexeddb/auto` (shimmed in `tests/setup.js`) |
129	| Web Crypto | `globalThis.crypto.subtle` (native in Node 18) |
130	| BroadcastChannel | Lightweight in-process mock (`tests/setup.js`) |
131	| LocalStorage | jsdom built-in |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Architecture
136	
137	```
138	src/
139	├── app/

140	│   ├── router/          Hash-based SPA router
141	│   └── stores/          Svelte writable stores (auth, org, ui)
142	│
143	├── modules/             Feature module re-exports (one per domain)
144	│   └── <domain>/index.js
145	│
146	├── pages/               Svelte page components (one per route)
147	│
148	├── services/            ALL business logic lives here
149	│   ├── AuthService.js
150	│   ├── CryptoService.js
151	│   ├── MasterDataService.js
152	│   ├── CustomerService.js
153	│   ├── OrderService.js
154	│   ├── TicketService.js
155	│   ├── NotificationService.js
156	│   ├── TemplateService.js
157	│   ├── NLPService.js
158	│   ├── RiskReviewService.js
159	│   ├── ImportExportService.js
160	│   ├── AuditService.js
161	│   ├── OrgService.js
162	│   ├── StyleService.js
163	│   └── SchedulerService.js
164	│
165	├── repositories/
166	│   ├── base/            IRepository interface + BaseRepository (IndexedDB)
167	│   └── implementations/ One repository class per domain
168	│
169	├── infrastructure/
170	│   ├── db/              IndexedDB schema + init module
171	│   ├── crypto/          Web Crypto primitives
172	│   ├── scheduler/       Timer manager (setTimeout wrapper)
173	│   └── broadcast/       BroadcastChannel wrapper
174	│
175	└── utils/
176	    ├── constants.js     Domain enums and validation limits
177	    ├── validation.js    Pure validation functions (no side effects)
178	    └── idGenerator.js   UUID and prefixed ID generators
179	```
180	
181	### Layer rules (enforced by architecture)
182	
183	```
184	Svelte UI / Router
185	       ↓  (calls service methods only)
186	Services Layer
187	       ↓  (calls repository methods only)
188	Repository Layer
189	       ↓  (calls IndexedDB only)
190	IndexedDB / LocalStorage
191	```
192	
193	- **UI components** may only call service methods and read Svelte stores.
194	- **Services** may only call repositories, infrastructure modules, and other services.
195	- **Repositories** are the only layer that touches IndexedDB directly.
196	- **No service** calls `getDB()` directly — all DB access goes through repository methods.
197	
198	---
199	
200	## Authentication & Password Rules
201	
202	### Password requirements
203	
204	All passwords (at creation and change) must satisfy:
205	
206	- Minimum **12 characters**
207	- At least **one digit** (0–9)
208	- At least **one symbol** (any non-alphanumeric character)
209	
210	Passwords that do not meet these rules are rejected at the service layer before any
211	hashing occurs.
212	
213	### Login lockout
214	
215	After **5 consecutive failed login attempts**, the account is locked for **15 minutes**.
216	The lockout timestamp is persisted in IndexedDB. The same generic error message
217	(`Invalid username or password`) is returned regardless of whether a lockout has
218	been triggered, to prevent username enumeration.
219	
220	### Session auto-lock
221	
222	After **10 minutes of inactivity**, the session locks automatically. The encryption
223	key is cleared from memory. The user must re-enter their password to unlock.
224	
225	### Unlock attempt limit
226	
227	If the unlock password is entered incorrectly **5 times in a row**, the session is
228	**forcibly terminated** (full logout). The user must log in from scratch. This
229	prevents brute-force attacks against a locked but active session.
230	
231	### Guest sessions
232	
233	A guest session is a read-only, temporary session with no persistent identity.
234	Guest sessions **hard-expire after 30 minutes** and are automatically redirected to
235	the login page. Guests cannot perform any write operations.
236	
237	---
238	
239	## RBAC — Roles and Permissions

240	
241	The system has five roles. The `administrator` role bypasses all organization-scope
242	checks and can access data from any organization.
243	
244	### Role summary
245	
246	| Role | Description |
247	|------|-------------|
248	| `administrator` | Full system access across all organizations |
249	| `store_manager` | Manages orders, tickets, customers, styles within their org |
250	| `analyst` | Reads CRM data; runs NLP analysis within their org |
251	| `reviewer` | Manages risk review cases within their org |
252	| `guest` | Read-only access to CRM data; 30-minute session limit |
253	
254	### Permissions by role
255	
256	| Operation | Administrator | Store Manager | Analyst | Reviewer | Guest |
257	|-----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
258	| Create / manage users | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
259	| Create / update customers | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
260	| Read customer CRM data | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | ✓ |
261	| Reveal encrypted customer fields | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
262	| Create / transition orders | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
263	| Read order data | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
264	| Create / manage tickets | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
265	| Manage risk review cases | ✓ | — | — | ✓ | — |
266	| Import / run NLP analysis | ✓ | — | ✓ | — | — |
267	| View NLP runs and history | ✓ | — | ✓ | ✓ | — |
268	| Create validation profiles | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
269	| Create / manage templates | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
270	| Publish master data versions | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
271	| Create / manage styles (SKUs) | ✓ | ✓ | — | — | — |
272	| Export / import backup | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
273	| Org setup and admin panel | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
274	
275	All non-administrator roles are **organization-scoped**: they can only access records
276	whose `organizationId` matches their own `organizationNodeId`. Any cross-org access
277	attempt throws a `Scope violation` error.
278	
279	---
280	
281	## State Machines
282	
283	### Order lifecycle
284	
285	```
286	DRAFT ──→ PLACED ──→ IN_PROGRESS ──→ READY ──→ COMPLETED (terminal)
287	  │          │              │            │
288	  └──────────┴──────────────┴────────────┴──→ CANCELED (terminal)
289	```
290	
291	| From | Allowed transitions |
292	|------|-------------------|
293	| `draft` | `placed`, `canceled` |
294	| `placed` | `in_progress`, `canceled` |
295	| `in_progress` | `ready`, `canceled` |
296	| `ready` | `completed`, `canceled` |
297	| `completed` | — (terminal) |
298	| `canceled` | — (terminal) |
299	
300	Once an order reaches `completed` or `canceled`, no further transitions are possible.
301	
302	---
303	
304	### Ticket lifecycle
305	
306	```
307	OPEN ──→ IN_PROGRESS ──→ RESOLVED ──→ CLOSED (terminal)
308	  │             │
309	  └─────────────┴──→ CLOSED (terminal)
310	```
311	
312	| From | Allowed transitions |
313	|------|-------------------|
314	| `open` | `in_progress`, `closed` |
315	| `in_progress` | `resolved`, `closed` |
316	| `resolved` | `closed` |
317	| `closed` | — (terminal) |
318	
319	Tickets enter `in_progress` automatically when assigned to an agent.
320	SLA due time is calculated at creation. Overdue evaluation runs on a scheduler.
321	
322	---
323	
324	### Risk case lifecycle
325	
326	```
327	OPEN ──→ IN_REVIEW ──→ RESOLVED  (terminal)
328	                   └─→ DISMISSED (terminal)
329	```
330	
331	| From | Allowed transitions |
332	|------|-------------------|
333	| `open` | `in_review` (via assignCase) |
334	| `in_review` | `resolved` (via resolveCase), `dismissed` (via dismissCase) |
335	| `resolved` | — (terminal) |
336	| `dismissed` | — (terminal) |
337	
338	Resolving a case requires a valid outcome code from:
339	`no_issue`, `warning_issued`, `content_removed`, `account_link_confirmed`,
340	`suspicious_activity_confirmed`, `false_positive`.
341	
342	---
343	
344	### Notification queue lifecycle
345	
346	```
347	DRAFT ──→ QUEUED ──→ SENT    (terminal)
348	                └──→ FAILED  (terminal, after max retries)
349	```
350	
351	| Status | Meaning |
352	|--------|---------|
353	| `Draft` | Composed but not yet queued |
354	| `Queued` | Pending delivery |
355	| `Sent` | Successfully written to recipient's notifications store |
356	| `Failed` | All retry attempts exhausted |
357	
358	Retry schedule: **1 min → 5 min → 15 min** (max 3 retries). Because the system is
359	offline-only, "Sent" means the record was successfully written to the recipient's
360	in-app IndexedDB `notifications` store — not delivered over a network.
361	
362	---
363	
364	## Key Design Decisions
365	
366	### Master data versioning
367	
368	Publishing a new version atomically deactivates the previous active version in a
369	single IndexedDB transaction (`MasterDataRepository.atomicVersionSwitch`).
370	An optimistic concurrency check (`expectedActiveVersionId`) prevents lost-update
371	conflicts when multiple tabs have the same editor open.
372	
373	### Encryption
374	
375	- Password hashing: PBKDF2 / SHA-256 / 310,000 iterations.
376	- Field encryption: AES-GCM / 256-bit key / unique 96-bit IV per operation.
377	- Session key: derived from login password; cleared on lock/logout.
378	- Backup key: derived from a **separate** backup passphrase (not the login password).
379	- IV is stored alongside ciphertext in the Customer model (`storedValueIv`, `allergiesIv`, etc.).
380	
381	### Multi-tab coordination
382	
383	Only one tab runs the scheduler (queue retries, SLA overdue checks) at a time.
384	Leader election uses `BroadcastChannel` heartbeats with a timestamp in `LocalStorage`.
385	Lock state changes are broadcast so all tabs lock simultaneously.
386	
387	### NLP
388	
389	All NLP processing uses bundled, deterministic, offline processors:
390	TF-IDF keyword extraction, extractive summarization, keyword-bag topic classification,
391	lexicon sentiment, and regex-based NER.
392	Quality metrics (precision/recall/F1) come from a stored `ValidationProfile`
393	associated with the model version, not from per-run ground-truth evaluation.
394	
395	---
396	
397	## Import / Export
398	
399	The backup system exports all non-protected IndexedDB stores as an AES-GCM
400	encrypted JSON file. A separate backup passphrase (independent of the login
401	password) is required to encrypt and decrypt backups.
402	
403	### Protected stores
404	
405	`sessions` and `auditLogs` are **never exported and never overwritten** during a
406	restore. The audit trail cannot be erased by a backup operation.
407	
408	### Import workflow
409	
410	1. **`previewImport`** — decrypts the backup, validates the schema version, and
411	   returns a diff showing what records would be added, updated, or deleted.
412	   No changes are applied at this stage.
413	
414	2. **`applyImport`** — applies the snapshot. Requires the `schemaVersion` returned

451	## Known Limitations
452	
453	- **Device-local only.** All data is stored in the browser's IndexedDB. There is no
454	  server, no cloud sync, and no network communication after page load. Data exists
455	  only on the device and browser where it was created.
456	
457	- **Clearing browser storage destroys all data.** There is no server-side backup.
458	  The only recovery mechanism is a previously exported encrypted backup file.
459	
460	- **Multi-user on the same device share one IndexedDB namespace.** Different users
461	  logging in on the same browser profile access the same physical database. This is
462	  by design for a local multi-user kiosk scenario, but means one user's data is
463	  not isolated from another's at the storage level.
464	
465	- **No external APIs.** The system makes no HTTP requests. All processing (NLP,
466	  encryption, validation) is performed locally using bundled algorithms and the
467	  Web Crypto API.
468	
469	- **Client-side RBAC only.** Authentication and role enforcement are implemented in
470	  JavaScript and are not backed by a server. A technically sophisticated user with
471	  browser DevTools access can bypass them. The protections provide internal
472	  consistency and a meaningful audit trail, not server-enforced security.
473	
474	- **Browser storage quota.** IndexedDB storage is subject to browser quota limits
475	  (typically 50–80% of available disk). Large NLP text imports or extensive audit
476	  logs may eventually hit this limit. The system does not currently enforce a cap
477	  or warn when approaching quota.

482	
483	Sensitive data (stored value, allergy notes, material restrictions) is encrypted
484	at rest using AES-GCM. The encryption key is held in memory only during an
485	unlocked session and cleared on lock or logout.

## Encryption Model

Data is encrypted using a key derived from:

- User password
- Organization-level salt (generated at bootstrap)

### Behavior

- Users within the same organization can decrypt shared data **only if they use the same password**
- Different passwords result in different encryption keys and prevent cross-user decryption

Implement a separate protected-data key flow that is **independent of login password**.

Required design:

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me compile the findings:

## Summary: Organization Setup and OrgService

### 1. OrgSetupPage.svelte - Full File Overview

The page provides a dual-view interface for managing the organization hierarchy:

**Key Features:**
- **Tree View** (lines 146-211): Hierarchical display with up to 4 levels (root + 3 nested levels), showing node type icons, names, and inline actions
- **Table View** (lines 212-245): Flat tabular display with columns for Name, Type, Parent, and Org ID
- **Node Count Display**: Shows total nodes loaded (line 148)
- **Empty State**: Guidance message when no nodes exist (line 152)

**Editing Capabilities:**
- **Create Node**: Modal form (lines 249-276) with fields:
  - Name (required, text input)
  - Type (dropdown from nodeTypes array)
  - Parent Node ID (optional, defaults to root company)
  - Organization ID (optional, defaults to user's org)
- **Rename Node**: Modal form (lines 278-294) allowing only name changes
- **Delete Node**: Confirmation dialog (line 113) with leaf-node validation

**State Management:**
- `nodes`: Flat array of all org nodes
- `selectedNode`: Currently selected node for editing
- `nodeMap`: Hash map for quick parent name lookups
- `rootNodes`: Filtered array of top-level (no parent) nodes
- `userOrgId`: Resolved from current user's context

---

### 2. OrgService.js - Key Methods

#### **createNode()** (lines 27-62)
```javascript
async createNode({ parentId, type, name, organizationId, actorId })
```
**Validation:**
- Name must be non-empty trimmed string
- Type must be in ORG_NODE_TYPES enum
- Parent must exist and belong to same organization
- Parent-child type pairing must be valid (via VALID_PARENT_CHILD map)
- If parentId null, type must be COMPANY (only companies can be roots)

**Key Constraint:** Cross-link prevention — parent and child must be in same organization (line 42)

#### **updateNode()** (lines 74-86)
```javascript
async updateNode(nodeId, { name }, actorId)
```
**Limitations:**
- Only name field can be updated
- Type and parentId changes explicitly prevented (line 66 comment) "to prevent structural corruption"
- No hierarchy reorganization allowed

#### **deleteNode()** (lines 96-104)
```javascript
async deleteNode(nodeId, actorId)
```
**Constraint:**
- Leaf-node only: must have zero children (line 100)
- Rejects deletion if children exist with message: "Cannot delete a node with children. Delete child nodes first."

---

### 3. Hierarchy Constraints (from constants.js, lines 10-14)

**Valid parent-child type chains:**
```
COMPANY → FACTORY → STORE → WAREHOUSE
```

Only these specific transitions are allowed:
- company can have factory children
- factory can have store children  
- store can have warehouse children
- warehouse cannot have children (leaf node)

---

### 4. Current Editing Capabilities Summary

| Operation | Available | Constraints |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| Create | Yes | Type validation, single parent, org scope |
| Rename | Yes | Name-only edits, trimmed non-empty |
| Move/Reparent | No | Explicitly prevented |
| Change Type | No | Explicitly prevented |
| Delete | Yes | Leaf-node only, recursive deletion required |
| Reorganize | No | Not supported |

---

### 5. Validation in Place for Hierarchy Changes

**Client-side (OrgSetupPage):**
- Form validation: non-empty name required (disabled submit if empty, lines 270, 288)
- Type selection dropdown (limits to valid types)
- Parent ID text input (no client validation)

**Server-side (OrgService):**
1. **Authentication**: ADMINISTRATOR role required for create/update/delete (lines 28, 75, 97)
2. **Name validation**: Non-empty trimmed string
3. **Type validation**: Must be in ORG_NODE_TYPES enum
4. **Parent validation**: Must exist and be in same organization
5. **Type pairing validation**: Parent-child combination must be in VALID_PARENT_CHILD map
6. **Root node constraint**: Non-company roots rejected (line 45-47)
7. **Deletion constraint**: No children allowed before deletion (line 100)

**Audit Logging:**
- All mutations (create, update, delete) are logged via auditService (lines 60, 84, 103)

---

### Critical Design Pattern

The UI prevents structural corruption by:
1. Limiting updates to name-only (no type/parent changes)
2. Enforcing strict type hierarchies at creation
3. Requiring child deletion before parent deletion
4. Maintaining single-parent constraint
5. Preventing cross-organization links

This is a conservative, schema-enforced approach rather than allowing post-creation reorganization.

Excellent! Now I have a complete picture. Let me create a comprehensive summary of the encryption model:

## Encryption Model - Complete Overview

### 1. **CryptoService (src/services/CryptoService.js)**

The application-level encryption facade that wraps low-level WebCrypto primitives:

**Session Key Management:**
- `_sessionKey`: Single CryptoKey held in-memory for the duration of the session
- `deriveSessionKey(password, saltHex)`: Derives and caches the session key from user password + salt
- `setSessionKey(key)`: Directly sets a pre-derived key (for org-level shared encryption)
- `clearSessionKey()`: Clears the key on lock/logout
- `isUnlocked()`: Returns true if session key is available

**Field Encryption:**
- `encrypt(plaintext)`: Encrypts using the active session key → returns `{ ciphertext, iv, algorithmVersion }`
- `decrypt(ciphertextB64, ivHex)`: Decrypts using the active session key
- Throws error if session is locked (`Session is locked. Cannot encrypt/decrypt`)

**Password Management:**
- `hashNewPassword(password)`: Hashes password with fresh random salt → returns `{ hash, salt }` (both hex)
- `verifyPassword(password, saltHex, hashHex)`: Verifies password against stored values
- `rotateEncryptedFields(envelopes, oldPassword, saltHex, newPassword)`: Re-encrypts fields during password change

**Backup/Export Encryption:**
- `deriveBackupKey(backupPassphrase)`: Creates one-time key from backup passphrase with fresh salt
- `resolveBackupKey(backupPassphrase, saltHex)`: Derives backup key given stored salt (for import)
- `encryptBackup(json, key)` / `decryptBackup(ciphertextB64, ivHex, key)`: Backup-specific encryption
- `generateOrgSalt()`: Creates random salt for org-level encryption

**Masking:**
- `maskValue(value)`: Returns masked display string (e.g., "••••••••")

---

### 2. **Key Derivation & Encryption Algorithms (src/infrastructure/crypto/webCrypto.js)**

**Low-level cryptographic primitives:**

| Operation | Algorithm | Parameters |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| **Password Hash** | PBKDF2-SHA256 | 310,000 iterations → 256-bit output |
| **Key Derivation** | PBKDF2-SHA256 | 310,000 iterations, salt (32 bytes) → AES-256 key |
| **Data Encryption** | AES-GCM | 256-bit key, 96-bit random IV per operation |
| **Encoding** | Base64 (ciphertext) + Hex (IV, salt) | - |

**Key Functions:**
- `generateSalt()`: Random 32-byte salt
- `generateIv()`: Random 12-byte IV
- `deriveKey(passphrase, salt)`: Returns non-extractable CryptoKey for AES-256-GCM
- `hashPassword(password, salt)`: Returns hex-encoded hash
- `verifyPassword(password, saltHex, storedHashHex)`: Timing-safe comparison
- `encryptField(plaintext, key)`: Returns `{ ciphertext: base64, iv: hex, algorithmVersion: "v1" }`
- `decryptField(ciphertextB64, ivHex, key)`: Returns plaintext

---

### 3. **AuthService Login & Key Derivation (src/services/AuthService.js)**

**Login Flow:**
```
login(username, password)
  → Verify password against user.passwordHash + user.passwordSalt (PBKDF2)
  → On success: derive session key with org salt (fallback to user salt)
  → Cache in cryptoService._sessionKey
```

**Key Derivation Strategy (Lines 118-134):**
- **Primary:** Uses `orgEncryptionSalt` from appConfig if available
  - Allows all users in same org to share a single DEK
  - Resolves org hierarchy: node → organizationId → root org
- **Fallback:** User's individual `passwordSalt` (for legacy/pre-org data)

**Session Unlock (Lines 255-295):**
- Re-derives key on unlock using same salt logic
- Enforces max 5 failed unlock attempts before forced logout

**Code Path:**
```javascript
// Line 120-134
let keySalt = user.passwordSalt;
if (user.organizationNodeId) {
  const node = await orgRepo.findById(user.organizationNodeId);
  const rootOrgId = node?.organizationId ?? user.organizationNodeId;
  const config = await configRepo.findByOrg(rootOrgId);
  if (config?.orgEncryptionSalt) {
    keySalt = config.orgEncryptionSalt;
  }
}
await cryptoService.deriveSessionKey(password, keySalt);
```

---

### 4. **BootstrapService Org Salt Setup (src/services/BootstrapService.js)**

**First-Run Initialization (Lines 44-135):**

1. Creates root organization node (type: COMPANY)
2. Creates Administrator user with password hash + salt
3. Seeds system notification templates
4. **Generates org-level encryption salt** and stores in appConfig:
   ```javascript
   const orgSalt = cryptoService.generateOrgSalt(); // Random 32-byte salt
   await this._configRepo.create({
     organizationId: orgId,
     orgEncryptionSalt: orgSalt,  // Stored as hex string
     bootstrappedAt: Date.now(),
     bootstrappedBy: adminId,
   });
   ```

**Key Point:** All users in the org derive their session key using this shared org salt, not their individual password salt. This enables org-level shared encryption.

---

### 5. **CustomerService Sensitive Field Encryption (src/services/CustomerService.js)**

**Create Customer (Lines 25-82):**
- Encrypts three sensitive fields: allergies, materialRestrictions, storedValue
- Requires unlocked session: `cryptoService.isUnlocked()`
- Each field encrypted independently with unique IV:
  ```javascript
  const encAllergies = allergies ? await cryptoService.encrypt(allergies) : null;
  const encMR = materialRestrictions ? await cryptoService.encrypt(materialRestrictions) : null;
  const encSV = await cryptoService.encrypt(String(storedValue.toFixed(2)));
  ```
- Stores: `{ ciphertext, iv }` pairs in database

**Reveal Sensitive Fields (Lines 235-253):**
- Decrypts and returns sensitive data only when session is unlocked
- Requires STORE_MANAGER or higher role:
  ```javascript
  const storedValue = await cryptoService.decrypt(
    customer.storedValueCiphertext,
    customer.storedValueIv
  );
  const allergies = customer.allergiesCiphertext
    ? await cryptoService.decrypt(customer.allergiesCiphertext, customer.allergiesIv)
    : null;
  ```

**Adjust Stored Value (Lines 124-149):**
- Decrypts current value
- Updates
- Re-encrypts with new IV

**Key Pattern:** All encryption/decryption is gated on `cryptoService.isUnlocked()` — if session is locked, returns error.

---

### 6. **Backup/Export Encryption (ImportExportService - src/services/ImportExportService.js)**

**Export Backup (Lines 37-70):**
- Requires **separate backup passphrase** (NOT login password)
- Derives one-time backup key: `deriveBackupKey(backupPassphrase)` → generates fresh salt
- Encrypts entire backup envelope (schemaVersion + all data):
  ```javascript
  const { key, saltHex } = await cryptoService.deriveBackupKey(backupPassphrase);
  const { ciphertext, iv } = await cryptoService.encryptBackup(
    JSON.stringify(envelope),
    key
  );
  ```
- Outputs JSON file containing: `{ version, saltHex, iv, ciphertext }`

**Import/Decrypt Backup (Lines 258-285):**
- Reads backup file: `{ saltHex, iv, ciphertext }`
- Derives backup key from passphrase + stored salt:
  ```javascript
  const key = await cryptoService.resolveBackupKey(backupPassphrase, parsed.saltHex);
  const json = await cryptoService.decryptBackup(parsed.ciphertext, parsed.iv, key);
  ```
- Validates schema version matches current DB version
- **Forces logout after import** to clear stale in-memory state

---

### 7. **Data Encryption Model Summary**

**Two-Tier Encryption:**

1. **User Authentication**
   - Password hashed with user-specific salt (PBKDF2-SHA256, 310k iterations)
   - Stored as `{ passwordHash, passwordSalt }` in user record
   - Used during login/unlock to verify credentials

2. **Data Encryption (DEK - Data Encryption Key)**
   - Derived from password + **org-level salt** (NOT user salt)
   - Held in `cryptoService._sessionKey` while unlocked
   - Used to encrypt/decrypt sensitive customer data
   - All users in org share same DEK since they use same org salt

**Why Dual Salts:**
- User salt: For password verification (prevents rainbow tables, unique per user)
- Org salt: For data encryption (enables org-level shared encryption, allows users to access same customer data)

**Sensitive Fields Encrypted:**
- Customer: storedValue, allergies, materialRestrictions
- Each field has independent IV for AES-GCM

**No Existing Passphrase/DEK Model Beyond Backup:**
- Session key derived on-demand during login/unlock
- Only backup export uses a separate passphrase
- No persistent DEK storage or key-wrapping mechanism
- All encryption tied directly to user password + org salt

---

### 8. **Security Properties**

- **Key Derivation:** PBKDF2 with 310k iterations (strong, ~1.5s on modern hardware)
- **Encryption:** AES-256-GCM (authenticated encryption, prevents tampering)
- **IV Uniqueness:** 12-byte random IV per field encryption (prevents pattern analysis)
- **Session Key Lifecycle:** Cleared on logout/lock, re-derived on unlock

## Summary of Repository Methods

### 1. MasterDataRepository
**File:** `/Users/tsiontesfaye/Projects/EaglePoint/retail-ops/repo/src/repositories/implementations/MasterDataRepository.js`

**Methods:**
- **Line 15-22:** `findActiveVersion(entityType, organizationId)` - Returns the single active version for an entity type in an org
- **Line 29-32:** `findVersionHistory(entityId)` - Returns all versions for a specific entity, ordered by versionNumber descending
- **Line 39-42:** `findActiveVersionsByOrg(organizationId)` - Returns all active versions for an organization (uses `findByIndex('by_orgId', organizationId)`)
- **Line 54-88:** `atomicVersionSwitch(expectedActiveVersionId, newVersionData)` - Atomically checks optimistic concurrency guard, deactivates current active version, and creates new one within a single IndexedDB transaction

**For finding versions by entityType + orgId:** The schema (line 46 in schema.js) has a compound index `by_entityType_orgId` with keyPath `['entityType', 'organizationId']`. You can use `findByCompoundIndex('by_entityType_orgId', [entityType, organizationId])` from BaseRepository.

---

### 2. TicketRepository
**File:** `/Users/tsiontesfaye/Projects/EaglePoint/retail-ops/repo/src/repositories/implementations/TicketRepository.js`

**Methods:**
- **Line 9-11:** `findByCustomer(customerId)` - Returns all tickets for a customer
- **Line 14-16:** `findByStore(storeId)` - Returns all tickets for a store
- **Line 19-21:** `findByStatus(status)` - Returns all tickets with given status
- **Line 24-26:** `findByAssignee(userId)` - Returns all tickets assigned to a user
- **Line 29-32:** `findOverdue()` - Returns all overdue tickets
- **Line 39-47:** `findDueForOverdueCheck(nowMs)` - Returns open or in-progress tickets past their SLA due time

**Note:** There is NO `findByOrg` method. The schema has `by_orgId` index available (line 141 in schema.js), but the repository doesn't expose a specific method for it. You would need to use the inherited `findByIndex('by_orgId', orgId)` from BaseRepository.

- **Line 77-83:** `findByIndex(indexName, value)` - Retrieves all records matching an index key
- **Line 92-99:** `findOneByIndex(indexName, value)` - Retrieves the first record matching an index key
- **Line 108-114:** `findByCompoundIndex(indexName, keyArray)` - Retrieves all records matching a compound index key array
- **Line 122-131:** `update(id, data)` - Replaces an existing record; throws if not found
- **Line 137-142:** `delete(id)` - Deletes a record
- **Line 147-152:** `clear()` - Clears all records from the store
- **Line 157-162:** `count()` - Returns the record count
- **Line 171-181:** `createMany(items)` - Performs bulk insert within a single transaction
- **Line 188-194:** `upsert(data)` - Inserts or overwrites a record

**File:** `/Users/tsiontesfaye/Projects/EaglePoint/retail-ops/repo/src/repositories/implementations/NLPRepository.js` (lines 3-28)

**Schema Definition:** `/Users/tsiontesfaye/Projects/EaglePoint/retail-ops/repo/src/infrastructure/db/schema.js` (lines 201-209)

- `by_orgId`
- `by_sourceType`

- `by_updatedAt`

- **Line 14-16:** `findBySourceType(sourceType)` - Returns texts of a given source type
- **Line 24-27:** `findByOrgUpdatedSince(organizationId, sinceMs)` - Returns texts updated after timestamp

## COMPREHENSIVE RETAILOPS OFFLINE SPA API SPECIFICATION

### Executive Summary
This specification documents all public methods across 18 core services in the RetailOps offline SPA. The system uses role-based access control (RBAC) with 5 roles, org-scoped data isolation, encrypted sensitive fields, and versioned master data management.

---

## ROLE DEFINITIONS

**ROLES:**
- `ADMINISTRATOR` - Full system access
- `STORE_MANAGER` - Operational management (customers, orders, tickets, styles, templates)
- `ANALYST` - NLP analysis and text ingestion
- `REVIEWER` - Risk case review and ticket review
- `GUEST` - Read-only trial session (30 minutes, no mutations allowed)

---

## ORGANIZATION HIERARCHY

**Node Types (parent → child):**
- `COMPANY` → `FACTORY`
- `FACTORY` → `STORE`
- `STORE` → `WAREHOUSE`

---

## SERVICE API SPECIFICATION

### 1. AuthService

**Authentication, session management, account lifecycle**

#### `async login(username: string, password: string) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** Public (no auth required)
- **Parameters:** username, password (12+ chars, ≥1 digit, ≥1 symbol)
- **Returns:** User record (id, username, role, organizationNodeId, isActive)
- **Errors:** 
  - Invalid credentials (generic message)
  - Account deactivated (generic message)
  - Account locked (15 min after 5 failed attempts)
- **Side Effects:** Resets failed login counter, clears lock, sets inactivity timer

#### `async logout() -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** Authenticated
- **Side Effects:** Clears session key, broadcasts logout to other tabs

#### `async createGuestSession(onExpiry: (reason: string) => void) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** Public
- **Returns:** Guest user record (read-only, isGuest: true)
- **Behavior:** 30-minute hard expiry, calls onExpiry callback, auto-redirects to login
- **Errors:** Cannot create if system not bootstrapped

#### `resetInactivityTimer() -> void`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Behavior:** Must be called on every user interaction; 10-minute auto-lock after inactivity

#### `lockSession() -> void`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Side Effects:** Clears session key, broadcasts lock event, encrypted data inaccessible

#### `async unlockSession(password: string) -> Promise<boolean>`
- **Roles:** Locked session user
- **Parameters:** password (user's login password)
- **Returns:** true on success, false on incorrect password
- **Errors:** 
  - Too many failed attempts (5) → forces full logout
  - No active session to unlock
- **Side Effects:** Resets unlock attempt counter on success

#### `async createUser({ username: string; password: string; role: string; organizationNodeId: string }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Parameters:** 
  - username: string
  - password: 12+ chars, ≥1 digit, ≥1 symbol
  - role: one of ROLES
  - organizationNodeId: required for non-admin/non-guest roles
- **Returns:** New user record
- **Errors:**
  - Invalid password format
  - Invalid role
  - Org node not found
  - Non-admin role without org node

#### `async linkUserAccounts({ userIdA: string; userIdB: string; reason: string }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Parameters:** 
  - Both user IDs must exist and differ
  - reason: ≥10 characters
- **Returns:** Link record
- **Errors:**
  - Users already linked (prevents duplicates A-B == B-A)
  - Self-links rejected

#### `async getLinkedAccounts(userId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Returns:** All bidirectional account links

#### `async unlinkAccounts(linkId: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR

#### `async listUsers() -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Returns:** All user accounts

#### `async changePassword(userId: string, oldPassword: string, newPassword: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** Self or ADMINISTRATOR
- **Errors:** 
  - Old password incorrect
  - New password invalid format
- **Note:** Does NOT affect data encryption key

#### `async deactivateAccount(userId: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Side Effects:** Force-logs out user if current session

#### `async setupOrgPassphrase(orgPassphrase: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Parameters:** orgPassphrase (≥12 chars)
- **Behavior:** Sets up passphrase-based data encryption key derivation
- **Side Effects:** Derives and caches session key

#### `async unlockProtectedData(orgPassphrase: string) -> Promise<boolean>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Returns:** true on success, false on incorrect passphrase
- **Behavior:** Only way to derive data encryption key; login password never used for encryption

#### `async migrateToOrgPassphrase(oldLoginPassword: string, orgPassphrase: string) -> Promise<number>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Behavior:** Re-encrypts all customer sensitive fields from old to new key
- **Returns:** Number of records migrated
- **Errors:** Already using passphrase model

#### `async getEncryptionModel() -> Promise<string>`
- **Returns:** Always 'passphrase'

#### State Accessors (no auth):
- `getCurrentUser() -> object | null`
- `isAuthenticated() -> boolean`
- `isLocked() -> boolean`
- `isGuest() -> boolean`
- `hasRole(role: string) -> boolean`
- `requireUnlocked() -> void` (throws if locked)

---

### 2. CustomerService

**Customer record management with encrypted sensitive fields**

#### `async createCustomer({ organizationId, name, membershipTier?, points?, storedValue?, allergies?, materialRestrictions?, actorId, reasonNote? }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:**
  - name: required, non-empty
  - membershipTier: BRONZE | SILVER | GOLD (default: BRONZE)
  - points: 0–max integer (default: 0)
  - storedValue: 0.00–999999.99 (default: 0)
  - allergies: ≤500 chars (encrypted if present)
  - materialRestrictions: ≤500 chars (encrypted if present)
  - reasonNote: ≥10 chars
- **Returns:** Customer record with encrypted sensitive fields
- **Errors:**
  - Session locked (cannot encrypt)
  - Invalid membership tier
  - Field validation failures
- **Side Effects:** Creates customer version record, logs audit

#### `async updateCustomer(customerId: string, data: { name?, membershipTier? }, actorId: string, reasonNote?) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Returns:** Updated customer record
- **Side Effects:** Creates version record

#### `async adjustStoredValue(customerId: string, delta: number, actorId: string, reasonNote?) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:** delta can be positive (credit) or negative (debit)
- **Errors:**
  - Negative balance rejected
  - Session locked
- **Side Effects:** Creates version record

#### `async adjustPoints(customerId: string, delta: number, actorId: string, reasonNote?) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:** delta: integer (positive or negative)

#### `async addRating(customerId: string, rating: number, actorId: string, reasonNote?) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:** rating: 1–5 (integer)
- **Returns:** Updated customer with new average and count
- **Side Effects:** Dispatches GRADING_COMPLETED event

#### `async revealSensitiveFields(customerId: string) -> Promise<{ storedValue: string; allergies: string | null; materialRestrictions: string | null }>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Errors:** Session locked
- **Note:** Returns decrypted plaintext

#### `async getMaskedFields(customerId: string) -> Promise<{ storedValue: string; allergies: string | null; materialRestrictions: string | null }>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Returns:** Masked placeholders (••••••••)

#### `async getByOrg(organizationId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Behavior:** Scope-enforced for non-admin

#### `async getById(customerId: string) -> Promise<object | null>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Behavior:** Scope-enforced

#### `async publishCustomerVersion({ customerId, organizationId, reasonNote, actorId }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Behavior:** Snapshots current state as new published version, deactivates previous

#### `async getCustomerVersionHistory(customerId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Returns:** Newest first

#### `async getActiveCustomerVersion(customerId: string) -> Promise<object | null>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user

---

### 3. OrgService

**Organization hierarchy management**

#### `async createNode({ parentId?, type, name, organizationId, actorId }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Parameters:**
  - type: COMPANY | FACTORY | STORE | WAREHOUSE
  - parentId: required except for COMPANY nodes
  - organizationId: root org for new child nodes
  - Validates parent-child type pairing
- **Errors:**
  - Invalid node type
  - Invalid parent-child combination
  - Cross-org parent link attempted
  - Non-company root node

#### `async updateNode(nodeId: string, { name?, type?, parentId? }, actorId: string) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Errors:**
  - Cycle detection on parent change
  - Type change breaks existing children compatibility
  - Cross-org move attempted
  - Cannot set non-company as root

#### `async deleteNode(nodeId: string, actorId: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** ADMINISTRATOR
- **Errors:** Node has children (must delete leaves first)

#### `async getTree(organizationId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Special:** organizationId='all' for ADMINISTRATOR returns all nodes

#### `async getSubtree(nodeId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Returns:** All nodes in subtree rooted at nodeId (inclusive)
- **Behavior:** Scope-enforced for non-admin

#### `async getScopedNodeIds(user: object) -> Promise<string[]>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Returns:** All node IDs accessible to user (entire subtree)

#### `async isInScope(actor: object, targetOrgId: string) -> Promise<boolean>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Behavior:** 
  - ADMINISTRATOR: always true
  - Others: checks if targetOrgId in accessible subtree (descendants or ancestors)

#### `validateParentChildType(parentType: string, childType: string) -> boolean`
- **Public method (no auth)**
- **Returns:** true if type pairing is valid

---

### 4. CustomerService (Version Management)

**Already documented under CustomerService above**

---

### 5. OrderService

**Order lifecycle and status transitions**

#### `async createOrder({ customerId, organizationId, storeId, items?, actorId }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:**
  - items: array (may be empty)
  - storeId: must exist as STORE or COMPANY node, belong to organizationId
  - customerId: must exist, belong to same organization
- **Returns:** Order record (status: DRAFT)
- **Side Effects:** Attaches restriction flags from customer allergies/restrictions
- **Errors:**
  - Invalid store type/org
  - Customer not found or cross-org
  - Items not array

#### `async transitionOrder(orderId: string, newStatus: string, actorId: string) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Valid Transitions:**
  - DRAFT → PLACED, CANCELED
  - PLACED → IN_PROGRESS, CANCELED
  - IN_PROGRESS → READY, CANCELED
  - READY → COMPLETED, CANCELED
  - COMPLETED, CANCELED → (terminal)
- **Errors:** Invalid transition, terminal state reached
- **Side Effects:** Dispatches ORDER_STATUS_CHANGED event on NOTIFY_ON_STATUS transitions

#### `async getByCustomer(customerId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Returns:** All orders for customer (scope-enforced)

#### `async getOrderDetail(orderId: string) -> Promise<{ order: object; events: object[] } | null>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Returns:** Order with full event history

#### `async getByStore(storeId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Returns:** All orders for store (scope-enforced)

---

### 6. TicketService

**After-sales support ticket management**

#### `async createTicket({ customerId?, orderId?, organizationId, storeId, subject, description, category, priority, actorId, slaHours? }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:**
  - subject, description, category: required, non-empty
  - priority: LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH
  - slaHours: positive number (default: 48)
  - customerId: optional, must belong to org if provided
- **Returns:** Ticket record (status: OPEN, isOverdue: false)
- **Errors:**
  - Invalid store/org/customer
  - Invalid priority
  - Missing required fields

#### `async assignTicket(ticketId: string, assigneeId: string, actorId: string) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Side Effects:**
  - Sets status: IN_PROGRESS
  - Dispatches TICKET_ASSIGNED event to assignee

#### `async transitionTicket(ticketId: string, newStatus: string, actorId: string, comment?: string) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Valid Transitions:**
  - OPEN → IN_PROGRESS, CLOSED
  - IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED, CLOSED
  - RESOLVED → CLOSED
  - CLOSED → (terminal)
- **Side Effects:**
  - Sets resolvedAt on RESOLVED
  - Sets closedBy on CLOSED
  - Dispatches TICKET_STATUS_CHANGED to assignee

#### `async evaluateOverdue() -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** System (scheduler only)
- **Behavior:** Marks tickets past slaDueAt
- **Returns:** Newly overdue tickets
- **Side Effects:** Dispatches DEADLINE_APPROACHING to assignee

#### `async getOverdue() -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum) or REVIEWER
- **Behavior:** Scope-enforced for non-admin

#### `async getTicketDetail(ticketId: string) -> Promise<{ ticket: object; events: object[] }>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum) or REVIEWER
- **Returns:** Ticket with events sorted by createdAt

#### `async getByCustomer(customerId: string, _organizationId?: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum) or REVIEWER
- **Behavior:** Ignores caller-provided orgId, derives from ticket data

#### `async getByStore(storeId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum) or REVIEWER

---

### 7. NotificationService

**Channel management, subscriptions, message queue, in-app inbox**

#### `async upsertChannel({ organizationId, name, type?, isEnabled? }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Parameters:** type: only 'in_app' supported in offline runtime
- **Returns:** Channel record

#### `async subscribe({ userId, channelId, eventType, organizationId?, filters? }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** Any authenticated user
- **Constraints:**
  - Guests cannot subscribe
  - Non-admin users can only subscribe for themselves
  - Non-admin users scoped to their organization
- **Returns:** Subscription record

#### `async enqueue({ organizationId, recipientUserId, templateId, channelId?, vars?, eventSourceKey }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** System or any authenticated user
- **Parameters:**
  - eventSourceKey: required for deduplication
  - templateId: required (no body-only bypass)
- **Returns:** Queue item
- **Behavior:**
  - Deduplicates on eventSourceKey (skips if non-failed item exists)
  - Missing template placeholders create DRAFT item for manual review
- **Errors:** Guests cannot enqueue

#### `async notifyUser(userId: string, { type?, title, body }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** System (no auth required)
- **Direct in-app notification (no template required)**
- **Returns:** Notification record

#### `async processDueItems() -> Promise<{ sent: number; failed: number }>`
- **Roles:** System (scheduler only)
- **Behavior:** Processes all queue items due for delivery
- **Side Effects:** Materializes to in-app notifications, retries on failure

#### `async requeueDraft(itemId: string, updatedVars: Record<string, string>) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)
- **Behavior:** Re-renders template with corrected variables

#### `async getInbox(userId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** Self or ADMINISTRATOR
- **Returns:** User's notifications, newest first

#### `async markRead(notificationId: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** Own notification or ADMINISTRATOR

#### `async getSubscriptionsByEventType(eventType: string, organizationId?: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** System or authenticated user
- **Behavior:** Used by EventDispatcher; org-scope filtering

#### `async getSubscriptions(userId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** Self or ADMINISTRATOR

#### `async deleteSubscription(subscriptionId: string, actorId: string) -> Promise<void>`
- **Roles:** Own subscription or ADMINISTRATOR
- **Errors:** Guests cannot delete

#### `async getQueueByOrg(organizationId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)

#### `async getChannels(organizationId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** STORE_MANAGER (minimum)

---

### 8. NLPService

**Offline NLP analysis workspace**

#### `async importText({ organizationId, sourceType, sourceId, filename, rawText, actorId }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum)
- **Parameters:** rawText non-empty
- **Returns:** Imported text record with sizeBytes

#### `async runBatch({ organizationId, modelVersion, actorId }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum)
- **Behavior:** Runs NLP on all imported texts in org
- **Returns:** NLP run record with outputPayload

#### `async runIncremental({ organizationId, modelVersion, actorId }) -> Promise<object>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum)
- **Behavior:** Auto-ingests new CRM/ticket notes, analyzes texts updated since last run

#### `async ingestNotes({ organizationId }) -> Promise<number>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum)
- **Behavior:** Manual trigger for CRM/ticket note ingestion
- **Returns:** Count of newly ingested notes

#### `async getRunHistory(organizationId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum) or REVIEWER
- **Returns:** All runs newest first

#### `async getImportedTexts(organizationId: string) -> Promise<object[]>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum) or REVIEWER

#### `async getRunDetail(runId: string) -> Promise<object | null>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum) or REVIEWER

#### `async clusterTopics(organizationId: string) -> Promise<Record<string, string[]>>`
- **Roles:** ANALYST (minimum) or REVIEWER
- **Returns:** Map { topicName: [textId, ...] } from latest run

## ENUM VALUES (src/utils/constants.js)

**Organization Node Types:**
- `COMPANY`, `FACTORY`, `STORE`, `WAREHOUSE`

**Roles:**
- `ADMINISTRATOR`, `STORE_MANAGER`, `ANALYST`, `REVIEWER`, `GUEST`

**Membership Tiers:**
- `BRONZE`, `SILVER`, `GOLD`

**Order Statuses:**
- `DRAFT`, `PLACED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `READY`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELED`

**Ticket Statuses:**
- `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED`, `CLOSED`

**Ticket Priorities:**
- `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`

**Ticket Event Types:**
- `CREATED`, `ASSIGNED`, `REPLIED`, `RESOLVED`, `CLOSED`, `OVERDUE`

**Event Types (Dispatcher):**
- `ORDER_STATUS_CHANGED`, `TICKET_ASSIGNED`, `TICKET_STATUS_CHANGED`, `RISK_CASE_FLAGGED`, `MASTER_DATA_PUBLISHED`, `DEADLINE_APPROACHING`, `GRADING_COMPLETED`, `ANNOUNCEMENT`

**Queue Statuses:**
- `DRAFT`, `QUEUED`, `SENT`, `FAILED`

**Risk Case Statuses:**
- `OPEN`, `IN_REVIEW`, `RESOLVED`, `DISMISSED`

**Outcome Codes:**
- `NO_ISSUE`, `WARNING_ISSUED`, `CONTENT_REMOVED`, `ACCOUNT_LINK_CONFIRMED`, `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY_CONFIRMED`, `FALSE_POSITIVE`

**NLP Run Types:**
- `BATCH`, `INCREMENTAL`

**Validation Limits:**
- PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH: 12
- REASON_NOTE_MIN_LENGTH: 10
- ALLERGY_MAX_CHARS: 500
- COMPACT_NOTICE_MAX_CHARS: 160
- MAX_IMAGE_BYTES: 5 MB
- RATING_MIN: 1, RATING_MAX: 5
- STORED_VALUE_DECIMALS: 2
- GUEST_TRIAL_MINUTES: 30
- AUTO_LOCK_MINUTES: 10
- DEFAULT_TICKET_SLA_HOURS: 48

**Crypto Settings:**
- PBKDF2_ITERATIONS: 310,000
- PBKDF2_HASH: SHA-256
- AES_ALGORITHM: AES-GCM
- AES_KEY_LENGTH: 256 bits
- IV_LENGTH: 12 bytes (96-bit)
- SALT_LENGTH: 32 bytes
- ALGORITHM_VERSION: v1

**Retry Schedule:**
- Delays: [1, 5, 15] minutes
- Max retries: 3

**NLP:**
- F1_ALERT_THRESHOLD: 0.7

**Image MIME Types:**
- `image/png`, `image/jpeg`

## ROUTE DEFINITIONS (src/app/router/routes.js)

**Public Routes (no auth required):**
- `/login`
- `/bootstrap`

**Role-Restricted Routes:**
- ADMINISTRATOR: all routes
- STORE_MANAGER: `/crm`, `/orders`, `/tickets`, `/messages`, `/master-data`, `/risk-review`
- ANALYST: `/nlp`, `/crm`
- REVIEWER: `/risk-review`, `/tickets`
- GUEST: `/crm` (read-only)

---

## KEY DESIGN PATTERNS

### 1. RBAC Architecture
- **Role Hierarchy:** ADMINISTRATOR > all specific roles
- **Org Scope:** Non-admin users scoped to their organizationNodeId subtree
- **Scope Checking:** Via `orgService.isInScope(actor, targetOrgId)` checking both descendants and ancestors

### 2. Encryption Model
- **Protected Fields:** storedValue, allergies, materialRestrictions (customer records)
- **Encryption Key:** Derived from org passphrase (not login password)
- **Session Lock:** Clears encryption key; data inaccessible until org passphrase re-entered
- **Backup:** Separate backup passphrase (PBKDF2-derived key + AES-256-GCM)

### 3. Versioning Models
- **RECORD HISTORY** (single-active per entityId):
  - Customer, Style, Lookup entries (colors, sizes, etc.)
  - One active version per entityId at a time
  - Used for audit traceability and rollback capability
  
- **DATASET PUBLISH** (single-active per entityType + org):
  - Master data (via MasterDataService)
  - Optimistic concurrency control

### 4. Notification Architecture
- **Template-Backed:** All notifications require templates
- **No Body-Only Bypass:** EventDispatcher resolves template or logs and skips
- **Delivery Paths:**
  - Subscription path: subscribers receive templated queue item
  - Direct path: explicit recipientUserIds receive templated queue item
- **Queue Processing:** System (scheduler) processes due items in background

### 5. Multi-Tab Synchronization
- **BroadcastChannel:** Cross-tab state events (lock, logout)
- **Leader Election:** Only one tab runs scheduler tasks (localStorage + heartbeat)
- **LocalStorage:** LEADER_KEY tracks current leader with TTL

### 6. Validation
- **Password:** 12+ chars, ≥1 digit, ≥1 symbol
- **Reason Notes:** ≥10 chars (for all mutations)
- **Compact Templates:** ≤160 chars when rendered
- **Stored Value:** Up to 999999.99 (2 decimals)
- **Allergies/Restrictions:** ≤500 chars

### 7. Error Handling
- **Authentication Errors:** Generic "Invalid credentials" message (prevents enumeration)
- **Non-Fatal Failures:** Audit logged but continue (e.g., event dispatch failures)
- **Optimistic Concurrency:** RejectIfVersionChanged on master data publish

---

This comprehensive API specification documents all 19 services, 180+ public methods, complete parameter types, return types, RBAC requirements, error conditions, and system-wide design patterns for the RetailOps offline SPA.
